en: Substance as power is the manifestation of itself through the arising and perishing of its accidents.
Active substance, as the original, is turned toward the contingent as toward something other, and is the cause which acts upon this other.
zh: 实体作为威力，是它自身通过偶性的产生与消逝而对自身的显现。
起作用的实体作为原始者，转向偶然者、也就是转向一个他物，并且是作用于这一他物上的原因。

en: The activity of substance consists in this: that it makes its original content effective, makes it a posited being which is in something external.
There is nothing in the effect which is not in the cause, and the cause is cause only in the effect.
zh: 实体的活动在于：它使自己原始的内容产生现实的作用，成为一个设定物，而这个设定物处在某个他物之中。
效果中没有任何东西是不在原因之中的，而原因只在效果中才是原因。

en: A falling brick is the cause of a person’s death, the swamp air of a region the cause of fevers; the one is at first only the cause of oppression, the other of excessive dampness.
But the effect in an actuality which still has other determinations becomes therein another result.
zh: 落下的砖石是某人死亡的原因，某一地区的沼泽气息是发热的原因；前者首先只是压迫的原因，后者是湿气偏盛的原因。
但是，在一个还有别的规定的现实者之中，效果会在那里变成另一个结果。

en: The effect is α) by means of something other, the cause; this, as activity, disappears in the effect; β) the other as cause has disappeared; but the effect is posited, it is in the other.
zh: 效果是：α) 借助一个他者、也就是借助原因；原因作为活动消失在效果之中；β) 作为原因的那个他者已经消失；但效果已被设定，它就在他者之中。

en: In form the cause is so different from the effect that the one is the actuality which is originally active from itself, whereas the other is posited and is in something other63); as a determination within another, actual being, it enters into a ratio with the remaining determinations of the same, and thereby acquires a shape which no longer belongs to it as effect.
zh: 在形式上，原因与效果如此有差别：前者是那原本从自身出发活动的现实性，后者则是被设定的、处在他者之中的63)；作为处在另一个现实者中的规定，它就与同一现实者的其余规定发生关系，并由此获得一种形态，这种形态不再作为它的效果属于它。

en: The cause passes over into effect, but conversely we go from the effect to the cause, and this regress belongs at first to external reflection.
Insofar as the cause itself has a determinate content, is contingent, and has to be posited as effect, we obtain the regress of a series of causes and effects into the infinite.
Conversely, insofar as that upon which the effect occurs is itself something original, it is a cause and brings forth its effect in something other; - the same series as infinite progression.
zh: 原因过渡为效果；但反过来，我们是由效果走向原因的，而这一回返首先属于外在反思。
由于原因本身有一个规定的内容、是偶然的、并且须被设定为效果，我们就得到一个由原因与效果构成的系列向无限处的回返。
反过来，就效果发生在其上的东西本身也是一个原始者而言，它就是原因，并在某个他者中产生出自己的效果；——这就是同一个系列，作为无限的进展。

en: External reflection: the cause is another thing than the effect, - is a difference of the thing; - absolute reflection the same content - the same thing - rain and dampness - is only an identity of the thing - 2. in the effect is what is in the cause; we know one from the other, - external identity - form and content or thing and content get confused; cause and effect is a difference of form; the cause holds as thing and then again only as form.
The effect has actuality only in the connection with that into which it is posited.
zh: 外在反思：原因是与效果不同的另一件事，——是这同一件事的差别；——绝对反思：同一的内容——同一件事——雨与湿气——仅仅是同一件事的同一；——2. 效果中所含的也就是原因中所含的；我们由一个东西认出另一个，——外在的同一；——形式与内容、或者事物与内容互相混淆；原因与效果是形式上的差别；原因先是作为事物有效，接着又只作为形式有效。
效果只有在与它被置于其中的那个东西相结合时，才具有现实性。

en: Insofar as an actuality takes the effect into itself, at the same time makes itself the cause and holds itself against the incoming action as against something external to it, it acts back, and the reaction is equal to the action.
zh: 就一个现实者把效果收进自身、同时又使自己成为原因，并把这种作用当作一个对它来说是外在的东西而相对抗而言，它就反作用，而反作用与效果相等。

en: Causality has something original, the cause, but this is transient, it goes out (hence one need not ascend absolutely from it to another cause), and so forth.
The effect posited in actuality B becomes a cause again; this is a negative deed, i.e. the effect is sublated, hence reaction.
zh: 因果性有一个原始者，即原因；但这原始者是过渡性的、会熄灭的（因此不必绝对地从它上升到另一个原因），如此等等。
被设定在现实者 B 中的效果又重新成为原因；这是一种否定性的作为，也就是说，效果被扬弃，因而有反作用。

en: The reaction occurs upon the first cause, which is thereby posited as effect {or made into a posited being}, whereby nothing else occurs than that it is now posited as what it is in itself, namely not something truly original but something transient.
zh: 反作用发生在第一原因上；它因此被设定为效果{，或被造成一个设定物}，这样一来所发生的无非是：它现在被设定成它自在所是的东西，即不是一个真正原始的东西，而是一个过渡的东西。

en: Reciprocal action therefore consists in this: that what is effect becomes mutually cause, and what is cause also becomes mutually effect.

Herein the true originality is present, since the cause indeed passes over into effect, into being posited, but with respect to the thing it remains the same and also with respect to form restores itself in its being posited.
zh: 所以，相互作用就在于：作为效果的东西彼此成了原因，作为原因的东西也彼此成了效果。
真正的原始性就在于此：原因固然过渡为效果、过渡为被设定，但在就事物而言它仍保持为同一个东西，并且在形式上也在它的被设定之中重新恢复自身。

en: Or reciprocal action is the mediation with itself in which the original determines itself or makes itself into a posited being, but therein reflects into itself and only as this reflection-into-self is true originality.
zh: 或者，相互作用就是与自身的中介；在这中介中原始者自我规定，把自己造成一个设定物，却又在其中对自身加以反思，并且正是作为这种对自身的反思，它才是真正的原始性。

en: The categories are simple determinations, but those which do not constitute the first elements of the determination are such only insofar as they are reduced to simplicity therein as opposed moments.

Now, as soon as such a category is predicated of a subject and at the same time those opposed moments are developed through the analysis, both are to be predicated of the subject; and thereby antinomical propositions arise, each of which has equal truth.
zh: 范畴是单纯的规定，但那些并非构成规定之最初要素的范畴，只有在它们作为对立的环节在其中被还原为单纯的情况下才是如此。
如今，这样的范畴一旦被谓述到一个主体上，同时又通过分析而展开那些对立的环节，那么这两者就都要被谓述到这个主体上；由此便产生出二律背反的命题，其中每一个都具有同等的真理。

en: Kant chiefly drew attention to the antinomies, but did not exhaust the antinomy of reason, in that he only set up some forms of it.
These are the following:
zh: 康德主要是让人注意到二律背反，但他并没有穷尽理性的二律背反，因为他只提出了其中若干形式。
如下：

29.en: I. Antinomy of the finitude or infinitude of the world according to time and space
29.zh: I. 关于世界在时间与空间上的有限或无限的二律背反

30.en: a) Antinomy of the finitude or infinitude of the world according to time
30.zh: a) 关于世界在时间上的有限或无限的二律背反

en: [Thesis: The world has a beginning in time.
zh: [命题：世界在时间中有开端。

en: Proof: Let us assume that the world has no beginning in time; then up to every given point of time an eternity has elapsed, and hence an infinite series of states of things in the world succeeding one another has flowed past.
But the infinity of a series consists in this: that it cannot be completed through successive synthesis.
Therefore [an infinite world-series is impossible, hence a beginning of the world in time is necessary.]
zh: 证明：假定世界在时间上没有开端；那么到任何一个给定的时点为止，都已过去了永恒，因而一个接一个相继的世界中事物状态的无限系列也已经流过。
但一个系列的无限性正在于：它不能通过逐次综合而完成。
因此[一个无限的世界系列是不可能的，因而世界在时间中的开端是必然的。]

en: [Antithesis: The world has no beginning in time and is infinite in time.
zh: [反命题：世界在时间中没有开端，并且在时间中是无限的。

en: Proof: Let us posit that it had a beginning; then before the beginning there would be a time in which it was not present, - empty time.
But in an empty time nothing can arise; for therein there is no condition of determinate being, and what exists has existent being as its condition or is only bounded by another existent being.
Therefore the world cannot have a beginning, but every determinate being presupposes another and so on into the infinite.]
zh: 证明：假定它有一个开端；那么在开端之前就有一个时间，在其中它并不存在，——空的时间。
但在空的时间里不能有任何东西产生；因为其中没有定在的任何条件，而定在者以定在者为条件，或者说，它仅仅是受另一个定在者的限制。
因此世界不能有开端，而是每一个定在都预设另一个定在，如此一直延伸到无限。]

en: The proofs of this antinomy reduce briefly to the direct opposition:
zh: 这一二律背反的证明简要地说可归结为直接的对立：

en: The world is finite according to time or has a boundary; namely the now is in the proof of the thesis the present instant in which the infinity has elapsed, i.e. would be finite.
zh: 世界在时间上是有限的，或者说具有一个界限；也就是说，现在在命题的证明中就是当下这一刻，在其中无限性已经流逝，即将是有限的。

en: Determinate being has no boundary in non-being, in empty time, but only in a determinate being; those which bound each other are also positively related to one another, and one has at the same time the same determination as the other; since therefore every determinate being is bounded through another determinate being and every one is at the same time a finite one, i.e. one over which one must pass, the progression into the infinite is posited.67)
zh: 定在并不是以非定在、以空时间为界限，而只以另一个定在为界限；彼此界限的这两者同时也正相互关联着，并且这一个同时具有与另一个相同的規定；因此，既然每一个定在都受另一个定在的限制，而每一个又同时是有限的，即那种必须越过去的定在，于是向无限处的进展就被设定起来了。67)

en: The true resolution of this antinomy [is] that neither that boundary nor this infinity is anything true in itself; for the boundary is something over which one must pass; and this infinity is only something for which the boundary always arises again and which beyond it is only an empty negative.
The true infinity is the reflection-into-self, and reason does not consider the temporal world, but the world in its essence and concept.
zh: 这一二律背反的真正解决[在于]，那个界限和这个无限性本身都不各自是真实的；因为界限是一种必须越过去的东西；而这个无限性不过是这样一个东西：界限总是重新在它身上产生出来，而它越过界限之后只是一个空洞的否定物。
真正的无限性就是那种对自身的反思，而理性所考察的不是时间性的世界，而是世界在其本质和概念中的样子。

43.en: b) Antinomy of the finitude or infinitude of the world in space
43.zh: b) 关于世界在空间上的有限或无限的二律背反

en: [Thesis: The world is bounded according to space.
zh: [命题：世界在空间上是有界限的。

en: Proof: Let us assume that it is unbounded; then it is an infinite given whole of simultaneously existing things, and it is in general an object.
Such a whole can be regarded as complete only through the synthesis of the parts it contains.
But this completion would require an infinite time which would have to be assumed as elapsed, which is impossible.
Therefore an infinite aggregate of existing things cannot be regarded as a given whole, hence not as a simultaneously given whole.
The world is consequently not infinite but enclosed within boundaries.]
zh: 证明：假定它是无限的；那么它就是一个由同时存在的事物构成的、给定的无限整体，并且它总归也是一个对象。
这样一个整体只有通过所含部分的综合才能被视为完成的。
但这种完成需要一段无限的时间，而它必须被假定为已经流逝，这是不可能的。
因此，一个由存在事物构成的无穷集合不能被视为一个给定的整体，因而也不能被视为一个同时给定的整体。
因此世界不是无限的，而是被限制在界限之中的。]

en: [Antithesis: The world is unbounded according to space.
zh: [反命题：世界在空间上是无界限的。

en: Proof: Let us assume that the world is bounded; then it is located in an empty unbounded space.
The world would therefore have a ratio to the empty space.
This would be a ratio to no object; but such a ratio, hence the ratio of the world to empty space, is nothing.
Therefore the world is infinite.]
zh: 证明：假定世界是有界限的；那么它就处在一种空洞的无界限的空间之中。
那么世界就会与那个空的空间有一种关系。
这就会是一种与任何对象的关系；但这样一种关系、也就是世界与空空间的关系，却什么也不是。
因此世界是无限的。]

en: The proofs of these antinomical propositions are likewise based essentially on direct assertions.
zh: 这些二律背反命题的证明其实同样建立在直接的断言之上。

en: The proof of the thesis reduces the completion of the simultaneously present totality of the spatial world to the succession of time in which the synthesis would have to occur, which is partly incorrect and partly superfluous; for in the spatial world the question is not of one following the other, but of one alongside the other.
Insofar as an elapsed infinite time is assumed, a now is assumed; just as much a here, i.e. a boundary of space in general, has to be assumed in space.
zh: 命题的证明把空间世界的、同时存在的总体性的完成归结为时间的相继，在这种相继中综合必须发生；这既部分地不正确，也部分地多余；因为在空间世界中所说的不是前后相继，而是彼此并列。
一旦假定一段已流逝的无限时间，就等于假定了一个现在；同样地，在空间中就必须假定有一个这里，也就是说，假定有空间本身的界限。

en: Since one has to go beyond the boundary in space in general, there is thereby posited the negative of the boundary (the opposite, the progression into the infinite); but since this is essentially only a negative of the boundary, it is conditioned through it, and in the same way as in the antithesis of the previous antinomy the infinite progression is posited.
zh: 既然必须越出空间中的界限而前，那么由此就设定了界限的否定者（即对立面、向无限处的进展）；但由于这一否定者本质上只是界限的否定者，所以它以界限为条件，并且正如前一二律背反的反命题那样，无限的进展被设定起来了。

53.en: II. Antinomy of the simplicity or the composition of substances
53.zh: II. 关于实体的单纯或复合性的二律背反

en: Thesis: Every substance consists of simple parts.
zh: 命题：每一个实体都是由单纯的部分组成的。

en: Proof: Let us assume that compound substances did not consist of simple parts; then, if all composition were sublated in thought, no compound part would remain and, since there are no simple parts, nothing at all would remain, nor any substance.

Thus not all composition can be sublated in thought; but the composite would again not consist of substances, for composition is only an accidental relation of them, without which they would have to exist as beings persisting for themselves.
Therefore the substantial composite must consist of simple parts.
zh: 证明：假定复合的实体不是由单纯的部分组成的，那么，如果一切复合性都在思想中被扬弃，就不会剩下任何复合的部分；而且既然没有单纯的部分，就什么也不剩下，连实体也不剩下。
所以并非一切复合性都能在思想中被扬弃；但复合物又不是由实体[们]组成的，因为复合性只是它们的一种偶然的关系，没有这种关系，它们就必须作为自在的、持存的存在者而存在。
所以，实体性的复合物必须由单纯的部分组成。

en: Antithesis: No composite thing in the world consists of simple parts, and nothing simple exists in it.
zh: 反命题：世界中没有任何复合的事物是由单纯的部分组成的，其中也不存在任何单纯的东西。

en: Proof: Let us assume that a composite thing consists of simple parts.

Since all external relation, hence also all composition out of substances, is possible only in space, so, from as many parts as the composite consists, the space which it occupies must also consist of as many parts.
Now space does not consist of simple parts, but of spaces.
Therefore every part of the composite must occupy a space.
But the absolutely first parts of everything composite are simple.

Since now everything real which occupies a space contains in itself a manifold situated outside one another, hence is composed68), the simple would be a substantial composite; which contradicts itself.
zh: 证明：假定一个复合的事物由单纯的部分组成。
由于一切外在关系、因而一切由实体构成的复合性都只有在空间中才是可能的，所以，既然复合物由这么多部分组成，它所占的那一空间也必定由同样多的部分组成。
然而空间不是由单纯的部分组成，而是由空间组成的。
所以复合物的每一个部分都必须占据一个空间。
而一切复合物最初的那些部分是单纯的。
既然一切占据空间的实在者都包含着一个处于彼此外在的多样者，因而是复合的68)，那么单纯者就会是实体性的复合物；这是自相矛盾的。

en: The proof of the thesis contains the direct assertion that composition is something contingent - an external relation - so that the simple is the essential. - The proof of the antithesis [contains] just as directly the assertion that substances are essentially spatial, hence composed.
zh: 命题的证明包含着直接的断言：复合性是一种偶然的东西——一种外在的关系——因而单纯者就是本质的。——反命题的证明同样直接地包含着这样的断言：实体本质上是空间的，因而是复合的。

en: - In itself [is] this antinomy the same as the preceding one: the opposition of a boundary and of going beyond the same.
zh: ——自在地[说]，这一二律背反与前一个相同：即一个界限与越出这一界限之间的对立。

63.en: III. Antinomy69) [on the opposition between causality according to laws of nature and freedom]
63.zh: III. 二律背反69)[关于依自然规律的因果性与自由之间的对立]

en: [Thesis: Causality according to laws of nature is not the only one from which the appearances of the world can be derived.
It is necessary to assume yet a causality through freedom for their explanation.
zh: [命题：依自然规律的因果性并不是世界的现象所能由以推出的唯一因果性。
为了解释这些现象，还必须假定一种由自由而来的因果性。

en: Proof: Let us assume that there is no causality other than according to laws of nature; then everything that happens presupposes a previous state, upon which it follows necessarily according to a rule.
But the previous state must itself be something which has happened, because if it had been there at all times, its consequence would also not only just have arisen, but would always have been.

Since therefore the causality of the cause itself is something which has happened, there results an infinite progression of the series of cause and effect, i.e. a series which is only incomplete, hence only a cause which is insufficiently determinate and grounding.
zh: 证明：假定除依自然规律的因果性之外没有别的因果性；那么一切所发生的事都预设一个先前的状态，并且按照一条规则必然地跟随于它。
然而，先前的状态本身必须是某个已经发生过的东西；因为如果它一向就存在，那么它的后果也不会是后来才产生的，而会一直存在。
既然原因本身的因果性是某个已经发生过的东西，那么就得出一个由原因与效果构成的系列的无限进展，也就是说，只是一个不完整的系列，因而只有一个未被充分规定、也不足以作为根据的原因。

en: One must therefore assume a causality which is absolute spontaneity, i.e. a free cause which of itself begins a series of appearances which runs according to laws of nature.]
zh: 因此必须假定一种因果性，它是绝对的自发性，也就是说，是一种自由的原因，它自发地开始一个依自然规律运行的现象系列。]

en: [Antithesis: There is no causality through freedom, but everything in the world happens merely according to laws of nature.
zh: [反命题：并没有由自由而来的因果性，世界中的一切都只依自然规律而发生。

en: Proof: Let it be posited that there is a causality according to freedom, namely a capacity to begin absolutely a state, and hence also a series of its consequences; then the determination of the spontaneity will also begin absolutely, so that nothing precedes which would determine the action of the freedom.

But every beginning to act presupposes a state of the cause which is not yet acting, and an absolutely first beginning of the action presupposes a state which has no connection whatever of causality with the previous state of the same cause, i.e. which in no way follows upon it.
Therefore absolute freedom is contrary to the law of causality.]
zh: 证明：假定有一种依自由的因果性，即一种能够绝对地开始一个状态、因而也是开始一系列后果的能力；那么自发性的规定也会绝对地开始，以至于没有什么先行于它、使自由的行为受到规定。
然而，每一个行动的开始都预设一个尚未行动的原因的状态；而行动绝对最初的开端则预设一个状态，它与同一原因先前的状态在因果性上毫无关联，也就是说，绝不以任何方式从它而来。
所以绝对自由与因果律相抵触。]

en: This antinomy rests in general on the opposition which the causal relation has in itself; namely the cause is α) an original thing and the first which moves itself; β) but it is a conditioned one through something upon which it acts, and then its activity passes over into the effect.
Thus it is nothing truly original, but must itself again be regarded as a posited being.

According to the first aspect an absolute causality, which through freedom, is assumed; but according to the second aspect the cause itself becomes something which has happened, whereby the progression into the infinite emerges.
zh: 这一二律背反一般地建立在因果关系本身所包含的对立上：即原因是 α) 一个原始的事物、第一个自身运动者；β) 但它又是通过某个它作用于其上的东西而成为有条件的，于是它的活动过渡为效果。
因此它并不是真正原始的东西，而本身又要被视为一个被设定者。
按照第一个方面，就假定一种由自由而来的绝对因果性；但按照第二个方面，原因本身就变成一个已经发生过的东西，由此产生出向无限处的进展。

en: The true resolution of this antinomy is the reciprocal action, that the cause which passes over into the effect has upon this again a causal reaction, whereby the first cause becomes effect, becomes posited being; in this mutuality it is thus contained that neither of the two moments of causality is an absolute in itself [one], but only this whole circle of the totality enclosed in itself, which is in and for itself.
zh: 这一二律背反的真正解决就是相互作用：原因过渡为效果之后，在效果上又有一种作为原因的反作用，于是第一原因就变成效果、变成被设定者；正是在这种相互性之中包含着这样一点：因果性的两个环节中没有一个是自在的绝对者[者]，而只有这个在自身中闭合着的总体性圆圈、这个自在并且自为的存在。

en: [Thesis: Something belongs to the world which is an absolutely necessary being.
zh: [命题：有某个绝对必然的存在者属于世界。

en: Proof: The sensuous world, as the whole of all appearances, contains at the same time a series of alterations.
Every alteration, however, stands under its condition, under which it is necessary.
Now every conditioned thing presupposes, in regard to its existence, a complete series of conditions up to the unconditional, which alone is absolutely necessary.
Therefore something absolutely necessary must exist if an alteration exists as a consequence.
But this necessary being itself belongs to the sensuous world.
For let us assume that it were outside the same; then the series of world-alterations would derive its beginning from it, without this necessary cause itself yet belonging to the sensuous world.

Now this is impossible; for since the beginning of a time-series can be determined only by that which precedes it in time, the highest condition of the beginning of a series of alterations in time must exist, since this series was not yet there; thus this highest condition belongs to time, hence to appearance or to the sensuous world itself; thus in the world itself something absolutely necessary is contained.]
zh: 证明：感性世界作为一切现象的整体，同时包含着一系列变化。
但每一变化都处在它的条件之下，在这一条件下它是必然的。
然而每一个有条件者就其存在而言，都预设直到绝对无条件者为止的一个完整条件系列，而唯有后者才是绝对必然的。
因此，如果变化作为一个后果而存在，就必须有某个绝对必然的东西存在。
但这个必然者本身也属于感性世界。
因为假定它在感性世界之外，那么世界变化的系列就会从它那里取得开端，而这个必然的原因本身却仍不属于感性世界。
然而这是不可能的；因为一个时间系列的开端只能由那在时间上先行于它的东西所规定，所以一系列变化在时间中的开端的最高条件必须存在，因为这个系列那时还不存在；于是这个最高条件就属于时间，因而属于现象或感性世界本身；因此在世界本身中就包含着某个绝对必然的东西。]

en: [Antithesis: There exists no absolutely necessary being, neither in the world nor outside the world, as its cause.
zh: [反命题：无论在世界中还是在世界之外，都不存在一个作为世界之原因而绝对必然的存在者。

en: Proof: Let us assume that the world itself or something in it is a necessary being; then in the series of its alterations there would either be a beginning which is unconditionally necessary and hence without cause, which contradicts the dynamical law of the determinacy of all appearances, or the series itself would be without any beginning and, though in all its parts contingent and conditioned, would nevertheless as a whole be absolutely necessary and unconditional, which contradicts itself, since the being of a multitude cannot be necessary if not a single one of its parts has a necessary being in itself.

Let us further assume that there is an absolutely necessary world-cause outside the world; then it would be what first begins the being of the world-alterations and their series; as soon as it began to act, its causality would belong to time and thus to the totality of appearances, and so would not be outside the world.
Therefore there is no absolutely necessary being either in the world or outside it.]
zh: 证明：假定世界自身或世界之中有一个必然的存在者，那么在其变化的系列中，就或者有一个开端，而这个开端是无条件必然的、因而是没有原因的——这与一切现象的规定性的动力学定律相矛盾；或者这个系列本身完全没有开端，虽然它的每一个部分都是偶然的、有条件的，但整体上却绝对必然、无条件——这又自相矛盾，因为如果其中没有任何一个部分具有自在的必然定在，一个集合的定在就不可能是必然的。
再假定在世界之外有一个绝对必然的世界原因，那么它就将是首先开始世界变化的定在及其系列的东西；一旦它开始行动，它的因果性就属于时间、因而属于现象的总和，所以它并不是在世界之外。
因此，无论在世界中还是在世界之外，都没有任何绝对必然的存在者。]

en: This antinomy contains on the whole the same opposition as the preceding ones.70) The conditioned presupposes a condition, and indeed an absolute condition which does not have its necessity in something other but is necessary in and for itself; but since it is in connection with the conditioned, it itself belongs to the sphere of the conditioned, to the world; according to the first aspect an absolutely necessary being is posited, according to the second a relative necessity and with it contingency. - But since it belongs to the sphere of the conditioned or is itself this whole sphere, it is itself only conditioned as such.
zh: 这一二律背反整体上包含着与前面几组相同的对立。70) 有条件者预设一个条件，而且是一个绝对的条件，这个条件并不是在他者之中拥有其必然性，而是自在自为地必然的；但由于它与有条件者处于联系之中，它本身就属于有条件者的范围、属于世界；按照前一方面，设定的是一个绝对必然的存在者，按照后一方面，设定的却是相对的必然性、因而也就是偶然性。——但是，由于它属于有条件者的范围，或者它本身就是这个完整的范围，它本身也不过就是有条件者而已。

en: The conditioned has a condition - contains the condition in its concept; absolutely separated; The condition contains the conditioned in its concept; is itself conditioned.
The conditioned has a condition or is conditioned
zh: 有条件者有一个条件——在它的概念中包含这个条件；绝对分开；条件在它的概念中包含有条件者；它本身也是有条件的。
有条件者有一个条件，或者说它是有条件的

en: The subjective logic no longer has the category and the determination of reflection as its object, but concepts.
The former is being in a determinacy, as boundary; the second is essence in a determination which is mediated through the presupposition of something other.

The concept, on the contrary, is the original, insofar as its determination is its reflection into itself; or it is a simple whole which contains its determinations in itself and from which all its determinations flow.
zh: 主观逻辑的对象不再是范畴和反思规定，而是概念。
前者是处在一种规定之中、作为界限的存在；后者则是在一种规定之中的本质，而这种规定是通过预设一个他者而被中介的。
而概念则是原始者，就其规定是它对自身的反思而言；或者说，概念是一个单纯的整体，它在自身中包含它的规定，并且它的全部规定都从它流出。

en: The subjective logic contains three main objects, 1. the concept, 2. the purpose, 3. the Idea; namely 1. the formal concept or the concept as such, 2. the purpose, the concept in relation to its realization or its becoming objective, 3. the Idea, the real or objective concept.
zh: 主观逻辑包含三个主要对象：1. 概念，2. 目的，3. 观念；也就是：1. 形式概念，或者概念本身；2. 目的，即概念与它的实现或它的客观化相关联时的概念；3. 观念，即实在的概念或客观的概念。

en: The formal logic has three objects: concept, judgment and syllogism.
zh: 形式逻辑有三个对象：概念、判断和推论。

en: The concept contains the moments of individuality, particularity and universality; it contains them as essential and distinguished determinations, and at the same time they are sublated in it, and it is the simple equality with itself.
zh: 概念包含个别性、特殊性和普遍性这三个环节；它把它们作为本质的、有差别的规定包含在自身之中，同时它们又在它里面被扬弃，而概念就是那种与自身的单纯相等。

en: Individuality is the negative reflection of the concept into itself, to which the determinations adhere as sublated, [as] moments, and which itself, as determined, excludes other determinations from itself or is absolutely determined.
zh: 个别性是概念在自身中的否定性反思；那些规定作为被扬弃的、作为环节，内在于概念之中；而概念本身由于是被规定的，便把别的规定从自身排除出去，或者说，它是绝对地规定着的。

en: Universality is the positive reflection of the concept into itself, in which that which is opposed does not exclude it, but rather it contains it in itself, so that it remains at the same time indifferent towards it and undetermined therein.
zh: 普遍性是概念在自身中的肯定性反思；在这种反思中，与之对立的东西并不把它排除，而是它自己在自身中包含这个对立者；因而它同时对这个对立者是漠然的，并在其中保持不确定。

en: Particularity is the relation of individuality and universality to one another; the universal is posited in a determination.
zh: 特殊性是个别性与普遍性相互之间的关系；普遍者被设定在一种规定之中。

en: Just as these determinations are distinguished from one another as moments of the concept, so too concepts of different content are distinguished as concepts of the universal, of the particular and of the individual.
zh: 这些规定作为概念的环节彼此如何相区别，内容各不相同的概念也就在「普遍者的概念、特殊者的概念和个别者的概念」这一点上相区别。

en: The universal subsumes or contains the particular and the individual, as the particular also holds the individual under itself; - the individual contains the particular and the universal, and the particular contains the universal in itself.
zh: 普遍者归摄、或者说包含特殊者和个别者，正如特殊者也同样把个别者置于自己之下；——个别者包含特殊者和普遍者，而特殊者在自身中包含普遍者。

en: The individual has the same determinations as the particular and the universal, or at the same time still further ones; the same holds of the particular in relation to the universal.
What therefore holds of the universal also holds of the particular and the individual; and what holds of the particular also holds of the individual.
But not conversely.
zh: 个别者具有与特殊者和普遍者相同的规定，或者同时还有更多的规定；特殊者与普遍者的关系也是如此。
因此，对普遍者成立的，对特殊者和个别者也成立；对特殊者成立的，对个别者也成立。
但反过来不成立。

en: The universal, however, is wider than the particular and the individual, and the particular is wider than the individual.72) The universal goes beyond the individual and the particular.
Namely the universal does not accrue to this particular and this individual alone, but also to others; and the particular likewise accrues to several individuals.
zh: 但是，普遍者比特殊者和个别者更宽，特殊者又比个别者更宽。72) 普遍者超出个别者和特殊者。
也就是说，普遍者不仅归属于这一个特殊者和这一个个别者，也归属于其他的一些；特殊者同样归属于若干个个别者。

en: The particular determinations which the same universal has under itself are co-ordinate with one another; those too are called co-ordinate which contain the same individual in themselves.
But in an individual, because it is exclusive, those determinations cannot be co-ordinate which are co-ordinate in the universal.
zh: 处在同一个普遍者之下的那些特殊规定彼此是并列的；包含同一个个别者的那些规定也同样叫做并列的。
但在一个个别者之中，由于它是排他的，那在普遍者中才并列的规定不可能是并列的。

en: The determinations which are co-ordinate in the universal are contradictory, insofar as the one has the essential meaning of being what the other is not, or insofar as they are opposed to one another as positive and negative.

They are contrary insofar as they are merely posited as different from one another, or insofar as the one still has a positive determination according to which it is not immediately opposed to the other.

The contradictory determinations alone, however, necessarily also have the moment of indifference towards the other, and the contrary determinations also have the moment of opposition attached to them.
zh: 在普遍者中并列的那些规定是互相矛盾的，就其中一个规定具有这样的本质意义：它就是那另一个规定所不是的东西；或者说，它们作为正与负而彼此对立。
它们是相反的，就它们只是被设定为彼此相异而言；或者其中一个规定还具有一个肯定的规定，凭这个规定它并不直接与另一个规定相对立。
唯有那些互相矛盾的规定必然地还带有对另一个规定漠然这个环节，而那些相反的规定自身也带着对立这个环节。

en: Strictly speaking, what is contradictory is not merely opposed as such - (as, strictly speaking, are also the positive and the negative) - but is a content, an immediacy which is at once positive and negative.
In the opposed there is the relation to something other, the whole content, the whole determinations.
The relation is here at the same time a repulsive reflection into itself.
zh: 严格说来，矛盾的并不仅仅是这样一种对立的东西——（其实正与负也是这样）——而是一种内容，是那种同时是肯定的又是否定的直接性。
在对立者之中有着对他者的关系，有着完整的全部内容和全部规定。
这种关系在这里同时是对自身的排斥性反思。

en: In the judgment the absolute unity in which the moments are in the concept is sublated; it is the relation of the determinations of the concept, insofar as each at the same time counts as its own, existing for itself and independent of the others.73)
zh: 在判断中，概念各环节所在的绝对统一被扬弃了；判断是概念诸规定之间的关系，就其中每一个规定同时都被看作自己的、独自存在并且不依赖于其他规定而言。73)

en: In the judgment otherness comes into the concept.
The judgment [is] something subjective; subject and predicate appear as indifferent, apart, external, and are first brought together by us, externally; is.
We have here a subject and here a predicate which we attach to it.
The judgment must become objective.
Separation (in the judgment) of subject and predicate, of thing and reflection. - The judgment kills the concept; men cannot suffer the judging upon themselves; it becomes power ...
[?] - because an individual determination; they [are] more than this; - he is also this.
zh: 在判断中，他在进入了概念。
判断是某种主观的东西；主体与谓词显得漠然、彼此分开、在外在的意义上，并且首先是由我们在外在的意义上把它们拉到一起的；是。
我们这里有一个主体，这里有一个我们附加给它的谓词。
判断必须成为客观的。
（在判断中）主体与谓词、事物与反思的分离。——判断杀死概念；人不能把这种判断施加在自己身上；它成为威力……
[?]——因为是单个的规定；它们[不只是]这一点；——他也是这一点。

en: The judgment contains 1. the subject as the side of individuality or particularity, 2. the predicate as the side of universality, which is likewise a determinate universality or a particularity, insofar as it contains only one of the several determinations of the subject; 3. the simple, contentless relation of the predicate to the subject: is, the copula.
zh: 判断包含：1. 作为个别性或特殊性这一侧的主体；2. 作为普遍性这一侧的谓词，它同样是一个规定了的普遍性或者说一个特殊性，因为它只包含主体的若干规定中的一个；3. 谓词对主体的单纯而无内容的关系，即：是，这就是连系词。

en: In relation to external reflection.
The subject is an object, an object about which one judges; the predicate is the determination of thought, the subjective -
zh: 就外在反思而言。
主体是一个对象、一个被判断的对象；谓词是思维的规定，是那个主观的——

en: The kinds of judgment designate the different stages in which the predicate raises itself to essential universality, or the external relation of subject and predicate becomes the internal relation of the concept. {The subject is once in immediate identity with the predicate; both are one and the same determinacy of content; but at another time they are distinguished.
The subject is a more manifold content than the abstract predicate and is in form a contingent. }
zh: 判断的种类标示着不同的阶段，在这些阶段中，谓词或者上升到本质的普遍性，或者主体与谓词的外在关系变成概念的内在一关系。{主体有一次是与谓词直接同一的；两者是同一个内容规定；但另一次它们却是相异的。
主体是比抽象谓词更多重的内容，并且在形式上是一个偶然者。}

123.en: a. Quality of Judgments or Judgments of Inherence
123.zh: a. 判断的质，或内在的判断

en: In the judgment the predicate is directly a property, namely some determinacy of the subject, of which it has several, and which has only the immediate form of universality.
Qualitative judgment.
zh: 在判断中直接地，谓词是一个属性，也就是主体的某个规定，主体有若干个这样的规定，而这个属性只具有普遍性的直接形式。
质的判断。

en: “This house is stone”; this is an individual determination of which the house has several; it does not express the inner universality of the house; - “this house is a thing”; it does not express its peculiarity.
It is stone, it has several such determinacies; stone is not its universal determination, - the one which contains what the house would be.
zh: 「这座房子是石头的」；这是一个单独的规定，房子有若干个这样的规定；它没有表达房子的内在普遍性；——「这座房子是一个物」；它没有表达房子的特性。
它是石头的，它有若干个这样的规定；「石头的」并不是它的普遍规定，——那个包含房子所会是的东西的规定。

en: It is 1. at first a positive judgment, since the universal has such a predicate at all.

This contains according to content the moment of determinacy and according to form the moment of universality; and the judgment means according to content: the individual is determined in such a way; according to form: the individual is universal.
zh: 它首先是 1. 肯定的判断，因为主体总归具有这样一个谓词。
这一判断按内容包含规定性这个环节，按形式包含普遍性这个环节；这个判断按内容说：个别者是这样被规定的；按形式说：个别者是普遍的。

en: α) The determinacy of content is αα) the distinction of the subject from others (red, not green); exclusion; ββ) judgment, the distinction of the subject from itself (red, not ...

[?] etc.); for the predicate contains only one of its determinations; the parting, the separation of the subject from itself. β) The determination of form, universality, αα) the equating of the subject with others; other things too are red; ββ) equating, making identical with itself; for the predicate is what the subject is; it is the being of the subject, the being-posited.
zh: α) 内容规定是 αα) 主体与其他的区分（红的，不是绿的）；排除；ββ) 判断，主体与它自己的区分（红的，不是……
[?] 等等）；因为谓词只包含主体的若干规定中的一个；主体与自身的分叉、分离。β) 形式规定、普遍性：αα) 主体与其他的等同；另一些东西也是红的；ββ) 等同、与自身的相同化；因为谓词就是主体所是的东西；它就是主体的存在，就是那个被设定起来的东西。

en: The judgment in both respects must [2.] also be expressed negatively, namely: 1. the individual is not so too, but differently determined; 2. the individual is not a universal, but a particular. - Negative judgment.
zh: 这两个方面上的判断[2.]也必须以否定的方式说出来，即：1. 个别者也不是这样，而是别样地被规定；2. 个别者不是一个普遍者，而是一个特殊者。——否定的判断。

en: In both respects this judgment is still positive; in the first, only some determinacy of the subject is negated, but it is left open that it has another from this universal sphere; in the other respect the negation is only the restriction of universality to particularity.
zh: 在这两个方面上，这一判断仍然是肯定的；在第一个方面，只是主体的某个规定被否定掉了，但仍然保留着它可以具有这一普遍范围中的另一个规定；在另一个方面，否定仅仅是把普遍性限制为特殊性。

en: The negative as well as the identical judgment can be reversed.
zh: 否定的判断和同一判断一样都可以颠倒。

en: But 3. the individual is also not a particular, but the individual is also only an individual74); and thus not merely some determinacy of a universal sphere is sublated from it, but every determinacy of the same and thus generally the sphere itself. - Infinite judgment, - in the positive form as the identical, in the negative form as an senseless judgment.
zh: 但是 3. 个别者也不是一个特殊者，而个别者同样只不过是一个个别者74)；因而从它那里被扬弃的，不只是这一普遍范围中的某个规定，而是该范围的每一个规定，因而是整个范围本身。——无限判断，——在肯定的形式上表现为同一判断，在否定的形式上表现为不合理、不成其为判断的判断。

138.en: b. Quantity of Judgments or Judgments of Reflection
138.zh: b. 判断的量，或反思的判断

en: The judgments of quantity contain a comparison of several subjects in relation to a predicate.
The quantitative judgment is 1. a singular judgment, whose subject is this thing and is supposed to have for its predicate a quality which accrues only to this subject.
zh: 量的判断包含着多个主体就某个谓词所作的比较。
量的判断是 1. 单称判断，它的主体是这一个东西，对谓词应当具有一种只归属于这个主体的质。

en: The particular judgment has some determinacies for the determination of its subject, whereby it is strictly speaking undetermined, and for every such positive judgment its negative holds just as much.
zh: 特称判断对主体的规定是若干个，因此它严格说来是不确定的，而且对每一个这样的肯定判断，它的否定判断也同样成立。

en: The universal judgment has allness as the determination of its subject, which is thereby a determinate, particular one.
zh: 全称判断以全体性作为对它主体的规定，而这个主体由此就是一个规定了的、特殊的主体。

en: Necessity begins in the universal judgment.
If all subjects have a quality, then necessity.
zh: 必然性在全称判断中开始。
如果所有主体都有一种质，那么就是必然性。

146.en: c. Relation of Judgments or Judgments of Necessity
146.zh: c. 判断的关系，或必然性的判断

en: The judgments of relation express an inner, necessary relation of the predicate to the subject.
zh: 关系的判断表达的是谓词对主体的一种内在的、必然的关系。

en: The categorical judgment has for its predicate the essence and the universal nature of the subject.
zh: 定言判断以主体的本质和普遍本性为谓词。

en: The hypothetical judgment contains, with a complete difference of the content of subject and predicate, the necessary relation of the one to the other.
zh: 假言判断在主体与谓词的内容完全不同的情况下，仍包含着两者之间的必然关系。

en: The disjunctive judgment has for its subject something as a universal sphere which is expressed in the predicate in its complete particularity or in its various determinations, which accrue to the universal taken as a whole just as much as they exclude one another with respect to the subject.
zh: 选言判断以某物为主体、把它作为一个普遍的范围，这个范围在谓词中或者以它完整的所有特殊性、或者以它各种不同的规定被表达出来，这些规定整体而言既同样归属于普遍者，又就主体而言互相排斥。

en: The modality of judgments consists in this: that the predicate expresses the adequacy or inadequacy of a subject to its concept or universal nature.
zh: 判断的模态在于：谓词表达一个主体与它的概念或普遍本性之间的相宜或不相宜。

en: The assertive judgment contains a mere assurance, insofar as the constitution of the subject which is compared with its essence, or this essence itself, is not expressed, and the judgment thus has merely a subjective warrant.
zh: 断言的判断包含着一种纯粹的断言，就主体那与其本质相比较的性状、或者其本质本身，并没有被表达出来，因此这个判断只是一种纯粹主观的担保。

en: This is good, because it is gold or has this or that determination.
zh: 这个是好的，因为它：是黄金，或者具有这样那样的规定。

en: Against the assurance of the assertive judgment therefore the opposite can just as well be asserted; the judgment becomes problematic and expresses only the possibility that a subject is or is not adequate to the concept.
zh: 因此，与断言的判断所作断言相对立的东西同样可以被主张；这个判断因此成为有问题的判断，它只表达一个主体与概念相宜或不相宜的可能性。

en: The subject is therefore to be posited as the universal with a determination which contains the constitution in which the adequacy or inadequacy of the same to its universal nature lies.
The subject itself thus contains this relation of the concept to determinate being, which the predicate expresses. - Apodictic judgment.
zh: 因此，主体要设定为一个普遍者，并带有一个规定，这个规定包含着那种性状，其中主体与它普遍本性之间的相宜或不相宜就位于其中。
主体本身以这种方式包含着概念对定在的这种关系，而谓词表达的就是它。——断言式的判断。

en: In the judgment the two determinacies of the concept are immediately related to one another; the syllogism is the judgment together with its ground.
The two determinacies are joined in the syllogism through a third, which is their unity. {The syllogism is therefore the complete positing of the concept.}
zh: 在判断中，概念的两个规定直接地互相关联；推论就是判断连同它的根据。
这两个规定在推论中由第三者联结在一起，而这个第三者就是它们的统一。{因此，推论是概念的完满设定。}

en: In terms of their determinate form, the two extremes of the syllogism are the individual and the universal; and the particular, since these two determinacies are united in it, is their middle. {If a determinacy A belongs to a determinacy B or does not belong to it, and determinacy B belongs to a determinacy C, then determinacy A belongs to C as well.}
zh: 就确定的形式而言，推论的两个极端是个别者与普遍者；而特殊者，由于这两个规定在它里面得到统一，就是它们的中项。{如果规定 A 归属于规定 B 或不归属于规定 B，而规定 B 归属于规定 C，那么规定 A 也归属于 C。}

en: Immediate syllogism in the Kantian antinomies: because space has a here, time a now (an infinity has elapsed up to the given point of time), it has a limit in general.
What the particular belongs to, the universal of the same belongs to as well.
zh: 康德二律背反中的直接推论：因为空间有一个这里、时间有一个现在（到给定的时点为止已经过去了一个无限），所以它总归是有界限的。
特殊者归属于谁，同一个体的普遍者也同样归属于他。

en: The relation of the two extremes (termini extremi) of the syllogism to the middle is an immediate relation; - it is a twofold relation and makes up two judgments (propositiones praemissae), each of which contains the moment of particularity, the middle (terminus medius).
The one premise further contains the moment of universality (terminus maior) as predicate (propositio maior), the other the moment of individuality (terminus minor) as subject (propositio minor).
The relation of the two extremes (conclusio) to one another is mediated.
zh: 推论的两个极端（termini extremi）与中项的关系是一种直接的关系；——这是一种双重的关系，它构成两个判断（propositiones praemissae），其中每一个都包含特殊性这一环节，即中项（terminus medius）。
其中一个前提还包含普遍性这一环节（terminus maior）作为谓词（propositio maior），另一个则包含个别性这一环节（terminus minor）作为主体（propositio minor）。
两个极端（conclusio）相互之间的关系则是被中介的。

en: qual. hypoth. disj.
Kinds: mathem.
Induction, analogy
zh: 质的、假设的、析取的
种类：数学的
归纳、类比

en: The mediation in the syllogism thus presupposes an immediate relation, and conversely the immediate relation is to be grounded and hence mediated; there is thus present the concept of an immediacy which is in itself mediation.
zh: 所以推论中的中介预设了一种直接的关系；而反过来，这种直接的关系又应当是有根据的，因而是被中介的；于是这里有了这样一种直接性的概念：这种直接性本身即是中介。

175.en: II. Purpose or the teleological concept
175.zh: II. 目的或目的论概念

en: In the purpose, what is mediated or is a consequence is at the same time an immediate first or ground.

What is brought forth through the mediation presupposes the bringing-forth and its immediate determinacy, and conversely the bringing-forth takes place for the sake of the result, which is the ground and thus itself the first determinacy of the activity.
zh: 在目的中，那个被中介的、作为后果的东西，同时就是一个直接的第一者或根据。
通过中介而被产生出来的东西，以产生及其直接的规定为前提；反过来，产生的目的是那个结果，而结果就是根据，因而本身就是活动的第一规定。

en: Teleological action is a syllogism in which the same whole in subjective form is joined with its objective form, the concept with its reality, through the mediation of purposive activity; or in which the concept is the ground of a reality determined through it.
zh: 目的论的行动是一个推论，其中同一个整体在主观形式下与它的客观形式、概念与它的实在性，通过合目的活动的中介而联结起来；或者说，概念是由它所规定的实在性的根据。

en: Purpose is the realization of a concept.
zh: 目的是一个概念的实现。

en: External purposiveness is this: insofar as a determinate being does not have its concept in itself, but is joined with it by another, a purpose, as its external form.
zh: 外在的合目的性在于：一个定在者如果不是在自身内部具有它的概念，而是由另一个东西、一个目的作为它的外在形式与它相联结。

en: Inner purposiveness is this: when a determinate being has its concept in itself and is at the same time, in itself, purpose, means, and the purpose which realizes itself and has been realized.
zh: 内在的合目的性在于：一个定在者如果在自身内部具有它的概念，并且在自身上同时就是目的、手段，以及实现着自身并已被实现了的目的。

en: The idea is the unity of the concept and reality, the concept insofar as it determines its reality for itself, or [the] actuality which is as it ought to be and contains its concept itself.
zh: 观念是概念与实在性的统一，是概念在它为自己规定其实在性的场合所是的东西，或者是[那]现实性：它如它所应当的那样，并且本身包含着它的概念。

en: a) The idea, insofar as the concept is immediately united with its reality and does not at the same time distinguish itself from it and stand out from it, is life; the same thing, presented [as] freed from the conditions and limitations of contingent determinate being, is the beautiful.
zh: a) 观念在概念与它的实在性直接合一、并且不同时又与它相区别、从中突出出来时，就是生命；同一个东西，呈示为[已经]从偶然定在的条件与限制中解放出来，就是美。

en: b) In the idea of knowing and acting, reality, the concept or the objective is opposed to the subjective, and their union is brought forth.
In knowing, reality lies at the ground as the first and as the essence, to which the concept is to make itself adequate so that it may be truth.
Acting, by contrast, has the concept lying at the ground as the essence and makes actuality adequate to it, so that the good may come to be.
zh: b) 在认识与行动的观念中，实在性、概念或客观方面与主观方面相对立，并且它们的统一被产生出来。
在认识中，实在性作为第一者、作为本质处于根据的地位，概念应当与之相相宜，以便它是真理。
与此相反，行动以概念作为本质处于根据的地位，并使现实性与它相相宜，以便善得以实现。

en: c) The absolute idea is the content of science, namely the contemplation of the universe as it is conformable to the concept in and for itself, or of the rational concept as it is in and for itself and as it is objectively or really in the world.
zh: c) 绝对观念是科学的内容，即对宇宙的考察：它与概念自在自为地相符合；或者是对理性概念的考察：它自在自为地是什么，以及它在世界中客观地或实在地是什么。

194.en: 8. Doctrine of right, of duty and of religion for the lower class76)
194.zh: 8. 面向下层阶级的法权学说、义务学说与宗教学说76)

en: The object of this doctrine is the human will, and indeed with respect to the relation of the particular will to the universal will.
As will, spirit behaves practically.

The practical behaviour by which it posits within its indeterminacy a determinacy, or in place of the determinacies present in it without its own agency other determinacies out of itself, is to be distinguished from its theoretical behaviour.
zh: 这一学说的对象是人的意志，而且是就特殊意志与普遍意志的关系而言。
精神作为意志而活动时是实践的。
那种实践的行为——精神在其中于自身的不定性里设定一个规定，或者把那些不是由它自己产生而现存在它里面的规定换成由它自己产生的另一些规定——应当与它的理论行为区分开来。

en: Consciousness in general is the relation of the self to an object, whether an inner or an outer one.
Our knowledge partly contains objects which we know through sensuous perceptions, and partly objects which have their ground in spirit itself.
The former make up the sensuous, the latter the intelligible world.
The juridical, ethical and religious concepts belong to the latter.
zh: 意识一般就是自我对一个对象的关系，不论那对象是内在的还是外在的。
我们的知识一部分包含我们通过感性知觉认识的对象，另一部分则包含在精神自身中有其根据的对象。
前者构成感性世界，后者构成可理解世界。
法权的、伦理的和宗教的概念属于后者。

en: In the relation of the self to the object, the self is 1. passive and the object is the cause of determinacies in me.
In this case the determinate representations which I have in me arise from the fact that objects which are immediately present make an impression on me.
This is theoretical consciousness.
Whether it behaves as perceiving or as imagination or as thinking, its content is always something already given and present, and in thinking it is the being-in-itself that is its content.

The self, by contrast, appears as practical consciousness when the determinacies of the self are not to be merely determinacies of its representing and thinking, but are to enter into external determinate being.
Here I determine things or I am the cause of changes in the given objects.
zh: 在自我与对象相互的关系中，自我 1. 是被动的，对象则是我内部诸规定的原因。
在这种情况下，我在自己内部具有的那些有规定的表象来自直接现存的对象对我造成印象。
这就是理论意识。
无论它表现为知觉、表现为想象力还是表现为思维，它的内容总是一个已经给出、已经现成的东西，而在思维中则是自在存在者构成它的内容。
相反，当自我的规定不仅是他的表象与思维的规定，而是应当进入外在的定在时，自我才表现为实践意识。
在这里，我规定事物，或者我是那些给定对象发生变化的原因。

en: The practical capacity determines itself in general internally, out of itself.

The content of its determinacies belongs to it, and it recognizes them as its own. - These determinacies are at first only inner ones and are therefore separated from the reality of externality; but they are to become external and to realize themselves.

This happens through acting, through which the inner practical determinacies acquire an externality, that is, an external determinate being. - Conversely this can also be viewed in this way: that an existing externality is sublated and made to agree with the inner determinacy.
zh: 实践能力一般是从自身出发、在内部规定自己的。
它的规定的内容属于它自己，它把这些规定认作自己的规定。——但这些规定起初只是内在的，因而与外在性的实在性相分离；然而它们应当成为外在的，并得到实现。
这通过行动而发生，行动使那些内在的实践规定获得一种外在性，即一种外在的定在。——反过来，这一点也可以这样来看：一个现存的外在性被扬弃，并被改造得与内在的规定相一致。

en: The inner determinacy of practical consciousness is now itself either a drive or the true will.

The drive is a natural self-determination which rests on limited feelings and has a limited purpose, beyond which it does not go; or it is the unfree, immediately determined, lower faculty of desire, according to which man as a natural being behaves. - Through reflection he also goes beyond the drive and its limits.

Through reflection he not only compares the drive with the means of its satisfaction, but also compares these means as well as the drives themselves with one another and with the purposes of his essence, and with the conclusion of reflection he either abandons himself to the satisfaction of the drive, or he holds it back and renounces it.
zh: 实践意识的内在规定现在本身要么是冲动，要么是真正的意志。
冲动是一种自然的自我规定，它建立在有限的感觉之上，有一个有限的目的，它并不超出这个目的；或者它就是那种不自由的、直接被规定的低级的欲求能力，人作为自然存在物就是按照它行事的。——通过反思，人也超出冲动及其界限。
人通过反思不仅把冲动与满足它的手段相比较，而且把这些手段以及冲动本身相互比较，并把它们与他的本质的目的相比较；于是他带着反思的推论，或把自己交付给冲动的满足，或把它抑制住并放弃它。

en: The true will or the higher faculty of desire is 1. the pure indeterminacy of the self, which as such has no limitation and no content given immediately by nature, and is indifferent in itself to every determinacy; 2. I can at the same time pass over to a determinacy and make this one or the other into mine, which I then put into actuality.
zh: 真正的意志或更高的欲求能力 1. 是自我的纯粹不定性，它作为这样的不定性既没有任何限制，也没有一个由自然直接现存的内容，并且自在自为地对任何规定性都无所谓；2. 我同时可以过渡到一个规定，把这一个或那一个变成我的规定，然后我把它置于现实之中。

en: The abstract freedom of the will thus consists in that indeterminacy or equality of the self with itself in which a determinacy is only in so far as the self makes it its own or posits it within itself, while at the same time it remains equal to itself there and can abstract again from every determinacy. - Various attractions, motives and laws may indeed be presented to the will from outside, but if man follows them, this happens only in so far as the will itself makes them its own and has decided upon them. - This is also the case with the determinacies of the lower faculty of desire, or with what comes from natural drives and inclinations.
zh: 所以意志的抽象自由就在于自我的那种不定性与自身等同之中：一个规定只有在自我把它变成自己的规定、或把它设定在自身之内时才是规定，同时自我在其中仍与自身保持相等，并且能够重新从每一个规定中抽象出来。——固然可以从外部把各种各样的诱惑、动机、法律摆到意志面前，但如果人遵循它们，那也仅仅是在意志本身把它们变成自己的规定、并为此下了决心的情况下才这样做的。——对于低级欲求能力的规定，或者对于出自自然冲动与倾向的东西来说，也是如此。

en: The will is guilty 1. insofar as its determinacy has been made its own by itself alone or belongs to its resolve: I have willed; 2. insofar as a will knows the determinacies which are brought forth through its action, as this lies in its resolve, or which are necessarily and immediately connected with it.
zh: 意志 1. 在下述情形负有罪责：它的规定只由它自己变成自己的规定，或者属于它的决心：我曾经想要；2. 在下述情形：一个意志知道那些规定——它们通过它的行动（行动如在它的决心中所包含的那样）被产生出来，或者必然地、直接地与行动相联。

en: The deed is in general the brought-forth alteration and determination of determinate being.
To the action, however, belongs only that which lies in the deed within the resolve or was in consciousness, which the will thus acknowledges as its own.
zh: 行为总的说来就是对定在所作的被产生出来的变化与规定。
但只有那在决心中属于行为、或曾在意识之中的东西，才算入行动；意志就是这样把它认作自己的东西。

en: The free will as free is further not bound to the determinacy and individuality by which one individual distinguishes itself from another, but it is the universal will, and the individual is according to its pure will a universal being.
zh: 自由意志作为自由的意志，同样不受那个使一个个体区别于另一个个体的规定性与个别性的束缚；相反，它是普遍意志，而个别者按其纯粹意志来说是一个普遍的存在。

en: The will can indeed take up into itself and make its own various external contents, that is, contents which do not proceed from its essence.

In that respect it remains equal to itself only in form, namely that it is conscious of being able to abstract immediately again from every content and to restore its purity, but not with respect to content and essence.
In that respect it is in general only arbitrariness.
zh: 固然，意志可以把各种各样的、外在的即不是从它本质中产生出来的内容接受到自身之内，并把它变成自己的。
在这方面，它只是就形式而言与自身相同，即：它知道自己能够立刻重新从每一个内容中抽象出来并恢复自己的纯净，而不是就内容和本质而言。
在这方面，它总的说来只是任意。

en: But in order that the will be truly and absolutely free, what it wills, or its content, can be nothing other than itself.
It can will only within itself and have itself as its object.
The pure will thus does not will any determinate content for the sake of its particularity, but that the will as such be free in its action and be let go, or that the universal will come about.
zh: 但为了使意志真正地、绝对地自由，他所想要的、也就是他的内容，除了他自己以外不能是别的什么。
他只能在自己本身之中想要，并把自己作为对象。
所以纯粹意志并不是为了它的特殊性而想要任何一个特殊的内容，而是要意志作为这样的意志在其行动中自由并被放开，或者要普遍意志发生。

en: The doctrine of right, of duty and of religion presents the more detailed determination and development of this general principle of the will.
zh: 对这个关于意志的一般原则作更详细的规定与展开，就是法权学说、义务学说与宗教学说。

en: Objects are the particular, what they are through their determinacy, - a sensuous object for example through its shape, size, weight, color, through the more or less firm coherence of its parts, through the purpose for which it is used, and so on.
If one now leaves out the determinacies of an object in the representation, this is called abstracting.
What remains is a less determinate object, or an abstract object.
But if in the representation I single out only one such determinacy, this too is an abstract representation.
An object left in the completeness of its determinacies is called a concrete object.
If I abstract from all determinacies, nothing remains to me but the representation of the wholly abstract object.

When one says "thing", one indeed means something determinate, but one is speaking of something wholly undetermined, since it is our thought which makes a real thing into this abstraction of a mere thing.
zh: 对象是特殊者，它们之所以是它们所是的，是通过自己的规定——例如一个感性对象通过它的形状、大小、重量、颜色，通过它各部分之间或多或少牢固的联结，通过它被用来达到的目的，等等。
如果人们在一个对象的表象中略去它的那些规定，这就叫做抽象。
剩下的就是一个规定较少的对象，或者说一个抽象的对象。
但如果我在表象中只取出这样一个单独的规定，这也是一个抽象的表象。
一个被保留在其规定的完满性之中的对象，叫做具体的对象。
如果我从一切规定中抽象出来，留给我的就只是那个完全抽象的对象的表象。
当人们说「物」时，他多半指的是某个有规定的东西，但他说的是某种完全无规定的东西，因为是我们的思想把一个现实的物变成了一个纯粹之物的这种抽象。

en: Sensuous perception is partly external and partly internal.
Through the external we perceive things which are spatially and temporally outside us and which we at the same time distinguish from ourselves.
Through internal sensuous perception we notice states partly of our body and partly of our soul.
One part of the sensuous world contains such objects and their determinacies as, for example, the colors, which have sensuous stuff as their foundation and which have received a spiritual form.

When I say "this table is black", I speak first of this single concrete object; secondly, the predicate black which I assert of it is a universal one, which no longer holds merely of this single object but belongs to several objects.
The black is a simple representation. - Of a properly concrete object we know immediately.
The immediate becoming aware is intuition.

A universal abstract representation, by contrast, is a mediated representation, because I know it by means of another, namely through abstraction or the leaving-out of other determinacies which are joined with it in the concrete. - A concrete representation is analyzed by expounding the determinacies which are united in the concrete.
The intelligible world receives its content from spirit, purely universal representations in general, e.g. being, nothing, property, essence and the like.
zh: 感性知觉一部分是外在的，一部分是内在的。
通过外在的感性知觉，我们知觉到那些在空间和时间上处于我们之外、并且我们同时把它们与自身区分开的东西。
通过内在的感性知觉，我们察觉到我们身体的状态和灵魂的状态。
感性世界的一部分包含着这样一些对象及其规定，例如颜色——感性事物是其基础，而颜色已经获得了一种精神形式。
当我说「这张桌子是黑的」时，第一，我说的是这一个具体的对象；第二，我断于它的谓词「黑」是一个普遍的谓词，它不再仅仅适用于这一个对象，而是归属于多个对象。
黑是一个简单的表象。——对于一个真正的具体对象我们是直接知道的。
这种直接的认识就是直观。
相反，一个普遍的抽象表象则是一个被中介的表象，因为我不是直接知道它，而是通过另一个知道它，也就是通过抽象或略去在具体中与之相联结的另一些规定。——一个具体的表象则是通过把在具体中统一起来的那些规定加以展开而被分析的。
可理解世界从精神那里获得它的内容，即总归是纯粹普遍的表象，例如存在、无、性质、本质等等。

en: The first source of our knowledge is experience.
Experience belongs in general to the fact that we have ourselves perceived something.
But a distinction must also be made between perception and experience.
Perception contains at first only a single object, which may now by chance be of such a sort and another time of another sort.
If I now repeat the perception and notice and hold fast in the repeated perception that which remains the same in all these perceptions, this is an experience.
Experience contains above all laws, that is, a connection of two appearances such that whenever the one is present the other also always occurs.
Experience, however, contains only the universality of such an appearance, not the necessity of the connection.
Experience teaches only that something happens or is present so and as it does, but not yet the grounds or the why.
zh: 我们认识的第一来源是经验。
经验一般地意味着我们自己知觉到过某物。
但还必须在知觉与经验之间作出区分。
知觉起初只包含一个单独的对象，它现在偶然可以是这样、另一次又可以是别的情况。
如果我现在重复这一知觉，并且在重复的知觉中察觉并固定下在所有这些知觉中保持相同的东西，这就是经验。
经验主要包含规律，即两个现象的这样一种联结：只要其中一个存在，另一个总是也随之发生。
但经验只包含这样一个现象的普遍性，却不包含这种联结的必然性。
经验只教给我们某物是如是、如怎样发生或存在，却还没有教给我们它的根据或那个「为什么」。

en: Since there are a great many objects about which we cannot ourselves make experience, e.g. the past, we must also rely on the authority of others.
Those objects too which we hold to be true on the authority of others are objects of experience.
What we believe on the authority of others is what is probable.

We often take what is really improbable to be probable, but precisely the improbable is often the true. - (An event proves itself above all through its consequences and through the manifold connection of circumstances of which we have experience ourselves.
The men who relate something must have credibility, that is, they must have been in such circumstances as to be able to have knowledge of the matter.
From their tone we can conclude their honesty, whether they are in earnest or whether they have some interest in it.
When authors write under the government of a tyrant and praise him, we see that this is flattery.
But when we hear someone relate something in which he himself is involved, we will presumably hear that he tells it to his own advantage.
But if someone highly praises a good quality or deed of his enemy, then we must rather believe what he says.)
zh: 由于存在非常多的对象，我们无法亲自对它们获得经验，例如过去；所以我们也必须依赖别人的权威。
那些我们凭别人的权威认为是真的对象，同样是经验的对象。
我们凭别人的权威所信的，是那个可能是真的东西。
我们常常把实际上很不可能的东西当作很可能的，但恰恰那个看似不可能的往往就是真的。——（一件事主要通过它的后果、通过种种情境之间的多样联结来证明自己，而我们对这些情境是有亲身的经验的。
讲述某件事的人必须具有可信性，也就是说，必须曾身处这样的情境，能够了解这件事。
从他们的口气中我们可以推断他们是否诚实：他们是否真心，还是另有某种利益。
如果作家在暴君的统治下写作并对他大加赞扬，那么我们看得出这是阿谀奉承。
但如果听到某人讲述一件他自己也牵涉在内的事，那么大概就会听说他是为了自己的利益在讲述。
但如果某人非常赞扬他的敌人的一项好品质或一个善举，那么我们反倒更应当相信他所说的话。）

en: Experience therefore teaches only how objects are constituted, not how they must be, nor how they should be.
This knowledge alone proceeds from the essence or the concept of the thing.
It alone is the true knowledge.
Since we learn to recognise the grounds of the object from the concept, we must also recognise the concepts of juridical, moral and religious determinations.
zh: 所以经验只教给我们对象是怎样的，不是它们必须怎样，也不是它们应当怎样。
这种认识只能从事物的本质或概念中产生出来。
只有这种认识才是真正的认识。
既然我们是从概念中学会认识对象的根据的，那么我们同样必须从法权的、道德的和宗教的规定中认识它们的概念。

en: With respect to what is right and good, we may in the first instance hold fast to experience in general, and to the external experience to begin with, that is, to the course of the world.
We can see what passes for right and good, or what proves itself to be right and good.

Here it is to be observed 1. that in order to know which actions are right or good and which are unright or evil, one must already beforehand have the concept of right and good; 2. that if one were therefore to hold fast to what the course of the world also shows as valid, nothing determinate would result on this point.
As regards the results or the experience one has, it would come down to the view one brings with one.
In the course of the world, because it is itself this heterogeneous occurrence, everyone can find confirmation for his subjective view, however different it may be.
zh: 在规定什么是正当与善的时候，我们首先可以一般地诉诸经验，而且首先是诉诸外在的经验，即诉诸世事的进程。
我们可以看到什么被当作正当与善，或者什么在实践中证明自己是正当与善。
对此要指出的是：1. 为了知道哪些行为是正当或善的、哪些是不正当或恶的，一个人必须事先就具有关于正当与善的概念；2. 因此，如果人们想要遵循世事进程所显示为有效的东西，那么关于这一点不会得出任何确定的东西。
就人们所获得的结果或经验而言，那要取决于人们带去的观点。
在世事的进程中——因为它本身就是这种各自不同的发生——每个人都能为自己的主观观点找到印证，不管这观点多么不同。

en: But secondly there is also an inner experience of the right, the good and the religious.
We judge through our heart or feeling that a mode of action is good or evil; we also have a feeling for religion; we are religiously affected.
What the feeling says as an approval or disapproval of it contains merely the immediate statement or the assurance that something is so or is not so.
The feeling gives no grounds and does not speak according to grounds.
What sort of feeling we have, approval or disapproval, is also merely an experience of the heart. - The feeling, however, is in general unsteady and changeable.
It is constituted one way at one time, another way at another.
The feeling is in general something subjective.
As an object is in the feeling, so it is only in me as a particular individual.
When I say: "I feel something so" or "something is so in my heart", I thereby say that it is so only in me.
I leave it undecided whether it is so in others as well.
If in something I appeal only to my feeling, then I do not want to go into grounds, and hence not to what is universal.
I then withdraw into myself and express only how the matter is in me, not how it is in and for itself, objective and universal.
The objective or the universal is the intelligible or the concept.
zh: 但其次还有一种关于正当、善与宗教的内在经验。
我们凭我们的内心或感觉判断某种行为方式是善还是恶；我们也对宗教有一种感觉；我们会受到宗教的感化。
感觉作为对它的赞成或反对而说出的东西，只是直接表明或担保：某物如此，或不如是。
感觉不给出根据，也不按根据来言说。
我们具有什么样的感觉——是赞成还是反对——同样只是内心的经验。——但感觉总归是无常的、易变的。
它在一个时候是这样，在另一个时候又另一样。
感觉总归是某种主观的东西。
一个对象在感觉中是怎样，它就只在我这个特殊的个体之内是这样。
当我说「我对某物有这样的感觉」或「某物在我的内心是这样」时，我这样说的意思是：它只在我这里是这样的。
我让它悬而不决：它在他人那里是否也是这样。
如果我在某件事上仅仅诉诸我的感觉，那我就不愿涉及根据，因而也不愿涉及普遍者。
于是我退回到我自己身上，只表达这件事在我这里如何，而不是它在自在自为的客观与普遍意义上如何。
客观的或普遍的东西就是可理解的东西，或者就是概念。

en: If one wants to know genuinely what a rose, a carnation, an oak etc. is, or wants to grasp their concept, one must first grasp the higher concept which underlies them, here the concept of a plant; and in order to grasp the concept of plant again, one must again grasp the higher concept on which the concept of plant depends, and this is the concept of an organic body. - In order to have the representation of bodies, surfaces, lines and points, one must have the representation of space, because space is the universal; bodies, surfaces etc., by contrast, are only particular determinations on space.

So future, past and present presuppose time as their universal ground, and so it is with right, duty and religion as well, namely they are particular determinations of the consciousness which is their universal ground.
zh: 如果人们要真正地认识一朵玫瑰、一株康乃馨、一棵橡树等等是什么，或者要把握它们的概念，那么首先就必须把握它们所依托的那个更高的概念，在这里就是植物的概念；而为了再次把握植物的概念，又必须把握植物概念所依赖的那个更高的概念，这就是一个有机体的概念。——为了具有关于物体、面、线和点的表象，人们必须具有关于空间的表象，因为空间才是普遍者；而物体、面等等只是空间上的特殊规定。
同样地，未来、过去与现在都以时间作为它们的一般根据；而法、义务与宗教也是如此，即它们是意识的特殊规定，而意识就是它们的一般根据。

en: In consciousness we normally have the object before us, or we know only of the object and not of ourselves.
But the I is essentially present in these things.
Insofar as we represent any object at all to ourselves, we have a consciousness, and indeed a consciousness of the object.

Insofar as we represent consciousness to ourselves, we are conscious of consciousness or we have a consciousness of consciousness. - In our ordinary life we have a consciousness, but we are not conscious that we are consciousness; we have much, and already something bodily, unconsciously; e.g. we possess the vital functions which belong to our self-preservation without yet having a consciousness of their more precise constitution, which we first acquire in science.

In the spiritual respect too we are much that we do not know. - The external objects of our consciousness are such as we distinguish from ourselves and to which we ascribe an existence independent of us.
The inner objects, by contrast, are determinations or capacities, powers of the I.
They do not exist alongside one another, but that in which they exist is the I. - Consciousness behaves either theoretically or practically.
zh: 在意识中我们通常是把对象摆在眼前的，或者我们只知道对象而不知道我们自己。
但在这些事情中本质地有自我在。
就我们总归只是设想一个对象而言，我们就有一个意识，而且是对对象的意识。
就我们设想意识而言，我们就是意识到意识，或者说具有对意识的意识。——在我们的日常生活中，我们有一个意识，但我们并没有意识到自己是意识；我们无意识地拥有许多东西，甚至已经包括身体的；例如那些属于我们自我保存的生命机能，我们虽然拥有它们，却还没有关于它们更详细性质的意识，那是我们只有在科学中才获得的。
在精神方面我们同样也是许多我们并不知道的东西。——我们意识的外在对象，是那些我们与自身区分开来、并归给它一种不依赖于我们的存在的对象。
相反，意识的内在对象则是自我的规定、能力与力量。
它们不是彼此外在的，而是它们所寓居的那个东西就是自我。——意识或者是理论地、或者是实践地活动着。

en: Theoretical consciousness contemplates what is and lets it be as it is.

Practical consciousness, by contrast, is the active consciousness which does not let what is be as it is, but brings forth changes in it and generates determinations and objects out of itself. - In consciousness, then, there are two things present, the I and the object: the I determined through the object or the object determined through me. - In the former case I behave theoretically.
I take up into me the determinations of the object as they are.
I let the object be as it is and seek to make my representations conform to it.
I have determinations in me, and the object also has determinations in itself.
The content of my representing is to be constituted as the object is.
The determinations of the object in itself are rules for me.
The truth of my representations consists in their agreeing with the constitution and the determinations of the object itself.
The law for our consciousness, insofar as it is theoretical, is not wholly passive, but it must direct its activity toward receiving the objectual.
Something can be an object for our perception without our having a consciousness of it on that account, if we do not direct our activity toward it.
This activity in receiving is attention.
zh: 理论意识考察那个存在着的东西，并让它如其所是。
相反，实践意识是能动的意识，它不让人所是的东西就这样存在，而是在其中产生变化，并从自身产生规定与对象。——因此在意识中有着两样东西：自我与对象，是自我由对象所规定，或者对象由我所规定。——在前一种情形下，我的活动方式是理论地。
我把对象的那些规定如其所是地接收进我之内。
我让对象如其所是，并力求使我的表象与它相符合。
我内部有一些规定，而对象自身内部也有一些规定。
我的表象的内容应当与对象如其所是的样子相合。
自在对象的那些规定就是我的规则。
我的表象的真理就在于：它们与对象本身的性质和那些规定相符合。
我们的意识就它是理论而言的那条规律并非完全被动的，它必须把其活动指向对对象性东西的接收。
某物可以是我们知觉的对象，但如果我们不把活动指向它，我们并不会因此有一个关于它的意识。
这种接收中的活动就是注意。

en: The representations which we acquire through attention we move within ourselves through the imagination, whose activity consists in this: that when we intuit an object it calls up for us the image of another object which is or was connected with the former in some way.
It is not necessary that the object to which the imagination connects the image of another be present; it can also be present only in the representation.
The most extensive work of the imagination is language.
Language consists in external signs and sounds through which one gives to be recognised what one thinks, feels or experiences.
Language consists in words which are nothing else than signs of thoughts.
For these signs writing in turn gives signs in the letters.

It gives our thoughts to be recognised without our having to speak at the same time. - Hieroglyphic writing differs from letter writing in that it comprehends whole thoughts within itself immediately.
In speech a certain tone is sensuously present.
We have therein the intuition of a tone.
We do not stop at this impression, but our imagination connects with it the representation of a non-present object.
There are thus two things present here, a sensuous determinacy and another representation connected with it.
The representation here counts merely as the essence and as the meaning of what is sensuously present, which is thereby merely a sign.
The given content stands opposed to a content which has been brought forth by us.
zh: 那些我们通过注意而获得的表象，我们是在自己内部借想象力加以推动的；想象力的活动就在于：当我们观照一个对象时，它为我们唤起另一个对象的图像，而后者与前者以某种方式相联结或曾经相联结。
想象力把另一个对象的图像联结其上的那个对象，不必是现存的；它也可以只在表象中是现存的。
想象力最广阔的作品是语言。
语言由外在的符号与声音构成，人们借此让人认出自己所想、所感或所体验的东西。
语言由词构成，词不过就是思想的符号。
对于这些符号，文字又以字母给出符号。
它使人认出我们的思想，而不必同时开口说话。——象形文字与字母文字的区别在于：它直接地把完整的思想包含在自身之中。
在言说中，某种声调在感性上是现存的。
我们在其中有对一种声调的直观。
我们并不停留在这个印象上，而是我们的想象力把一个非现存对象的表象联结其上。
因此这里有两样东西：一个感性的规定，以及一个联结其上的另一些表象。
表象在这里仅仅作为感性现存者的本质与意义而有效；这个感性现存者由此只是一个单纯的符号。
那个被给予的内容与那个由我们产生出来的内容相对立。

en: In common life one confuses representation and thinking, and we also call that thinking which is only a representation of the imagination.
In the representation we also have the thing before us according to its external, inessential determinate being.
In thinking, by contrast, we separate the external, merely inessential from the thing and raise the thing up only in its essence.
Thinking penetrates through the external appearance to the inner nature of the thing and makes it its object.
It leaves out the contingent of a thing.
It does not take a thing as it is as immediate appearance, but separates the inessential from the essential and thus abstracts from it. - In intuition we have individual objects before us.
Thinking relates these to one another or compares them.

In the comparison it picks out what they have in common and leaves out that whereby they differ from one another, and thereby obtains universal representations. - The universal representation contains less determinacy than the individual object which falls under this universal, because one obtains the universal precisely only by leaving out the individual.
The universal, by contrast, comprehends more under itself or has a far greater compass.
Insofar as thinking brings forth a universal object, the activity of abstracting accrues to it and with it the form of universality, as, for example, in the universal object "man".
But the content of the universal object does not accrue to thinking as abstracting; rather it is given to thinking and is present in itself independently of it.
zh: 在日常生活中，人们混淆表象与思维，把只是想象力的表象的东西也叫作思维。
在表象中，我们甚至也按照一个事物外在的、非本质的定在样子把它摆在眼前。
而在思维中，我们把外在的、纯粹非本质的东西从事物中区分出去，只在它的本质中把事物突出出来。
思维穿过外在的现象深入事物内在的本性，并把它变成自己的对象。
它略去一个事物上偶然的东西。
它所把握的不是一个事物作为直接现象的那个样子，而是把非本质的东西与本质的东西区分开来，因而对它进行抽象。——在直观中，我们面前有个别对象。
思维把它们相互联系起来，或者说，把它们加以比较。
在比较中，它把它们共同具有的东西突出出来，略去它们彼此相区别的东西，从而得到普遍的表象。——普遍的表象比那个归入这一普遍者的个别对象包含更少的规定性，因为恰恰只有通过略去个别者才能得到普遍者。
相反，普遍者包含在自身之下的更多，或者说具有远为宽大的范围。
思维在产生出一个普遍对象时，就获得了抽象这一活动以及由此而来的普遍性形式，例如在「人」这个普遍对象中。
但普遍对象的内容并不作为抽象而归于思维；它是给予思维的，并且自在自为地独立于思维而现存的。

en: Many various determinations accrue to thinking which express a connection between the manifold appearances which is universal and necessary.
The connection as it is in sensuous intuition is only an external or contingent one, which can be so or not be so.
A stone, for example, by its falling makes an impression in a soft mass.
In sensuous intuition there lies the falling of the stone and that thereupon, in time, a hollow is present in the mass where the stone touched it.
These two appearances, the falling of the stone and the hollowing of the mass, have succeeded one another in time.
Yet this connection contains no necessity yet; on the contrary, in terms of the expression, under the same conditions the one could happen and the other not follow upon it.

If, by contrast, the relation of these two appearances to one another determines itself as a connection of cause and effect or as causality, then this connection is necessary, or a connection of understanding.
It lies therein that, if under the same conditions the one happens, the other is contained in it.
zh: 此外归于思维的还有多种多样的规定，它们表达出各种现象之间一种普遍而必然的联结。
这种联结在感性直观中的样子，只是一种外在的或偶然的联结，它可能是这样，也可能不是这样。
例如一块石头因落下而在柔软的物质上留下一个印痕。
在感性直观中有着石头的落下，以及随之在时间上于石头接触处的那团物质中出现了一个凹坑。
这两个现象——石头的落下与物质的凹陷——在时间上是相继发生的。
但这种联结还不包含必然性；按其表述来说，在同样的条件下这一个可能发生，而另一个也可能不随之发生。
但如果这两个现象之间的关系把自己规定为原因与效果的联结，或者规定为因果性，那么这种联结就是必然的，或者说就是知性的联结。
它在于：在同样的条件下这一个发生时，另一个已经包含在其中。

en: These determinations are forms of thinking.
Spirit posits them only out of itself, but they are at the same time determinations of the being.
We come upon what ground and consequence, what inner and outer, what essential or inessential is, only by thinking it through.
Spirit is not conscious in this of positing these determinations arbitrarily; rather it expresses in them something which is present in itself without its agency.
zh: 这些规定是思维的形式。
精神只是从自身出发设定它们，但它们同时也是存在者的规定。
我们只有通过深思才想到：什么是根据与后果、什么是内在与外在、什么是本质的与非本质的。
精神并没有意识到自己是在任意地设定这些规定，而是在其中表达出某种不假它助力便自在自为地现存的东西。

en: In general, so far as it is said that spirit receives determinations, the indeterminacy of the I or of spirit is presupposed.
The determinations of spirit belong to it, even if it has received them from other objects.

Insofar as something is in it which, as a content independent of it, does not come from it, the form nevertheless always belongs to it; e.g. with the imagination the material does indeed come from intuition, but the form consists in the way in which this material has been connected otherwise than it was originally present in intuition.
In a pure representation, e.g. that of the animal, the determinate content of experience belongs to it, but the universal in it is the form which comes from spirit.
zh: 一般说来，就谈到精神获得规定而言，是以自我或精神的不定性为前提的。
精神的那些规定属于它自己，即使它是从别的对象那里获得它们的。
就其中有着某种作为不依赖于它的内容而非由它而来的东西而言，但形式始终属于它；例如在想象力中，材料固然来自直观，但形式在于这个材料被联结得与它在直观中原本存在的样子不同。
在一个纯粹的表象中，例如动物的表象，那个有规定的内容属于经验，但其中的普遍者就是来自精神的形式。

en: This form is therefore the proper determining of spirit.
In the theoretical capacity, then, it makes the essential difference that only the form lies in the determining of spirit, whereas in the practical the content too comes from spirit.
In right, for example, the content is personal freedom.
This belongs to spirit.
The practical capacity recognises determinations as its own insofar as it wills them at all.
Even if they appear as alien determinations or as given ones, they must cease to be alien determinations insofar as I will them.
I transform the content into my own and posit it through myself.
zh: 所以这种形式就是精神自己的规定活动。
于是，在理论能力中，本质区别在于只有形式位于精神的设定活动之中；而在实践能力中，内容同样来自精神。
例如在法中，内容就是人格自由。
这种自由属于精神。
实践能力把规定认作自己的规定，就在于它总之愿意它们。
即使它们显得是外来的规定或是被给予的规定，但只要我愿意它们，它们就必须不再是外来的规定。
我把内容转化为我的东西，通过我自己把它设定出来。

en: The theoretical capacity begins with a determinate being, something present, something external, and makes it into a representation.
The practical, by contrast, begins with an inner determinacy.
This is called resolve, design and guidance, and it makes the inner really external, gives it a determinate being.
This transition from an inner determinacy to externality is called action.
zh: 理论能力从一个定在着的、现存的、外在的东西出发，把它变成一个表象。
实践能力则从一个内在的规定出发。
这叫做决心、意图与引导，它使内在的东西真正成为外在的，给它一个定在。
这种从一个内在规定向外在性的过渡叫做行动。

en: Action is in general a union of the inner and the outer.

The inner determinacy from which it begins is to be sublated in terms of form, namely insofar as it is merely inner, and is to become external; the content of this determinacy is to remain in the process; e.g. the design to build a house is an inner determinacy whose form consists in being as yet only a design; its content comprehends the plan of the house.
If now here the form is sublated, the content nevertheless remains.
The house which is to be built according to the design and the house which is built according to the plan are the same house.
zh: 行动总的说来是内在与外在的统一。
行动由之而起的那个内在规定，就形式而言——即就它还仅仅是内在的这一点而言——应当被扬弃并成为外在的；而这一规定的内容应当在这过程中保留下来；例如「要造一所房子」这一意图是一个内在规定，其形式在于它还仅仅是一个意图；它的内容则包含房子的设计。
现在这里形式虽然被扬弃了，内容却仍然保留。
按照意图而将要建造的房子，与按照设计而建造的房子，是同一所房子。

en: Conversely action is just as much a sublation of the external in so far as it is immediately present; e.g. for the building of a house the soil, stones, wood and the remaining materials are altered in manifold ways.
The shape of the external is made otherwise.
It is brought into a quite different connection than it was before.
This alteration takes place in accordance with a purpose, namely with the plan of the house, with which the external is thus made to agree.
zh: 反过来，行动同样是对外在之物的扬弃，就它是直接现存的那样；例如为建造一所房子，土地、石头、木材以及其余材料都以多种多样的方式被改变。
外在者的形态被改造得不一样了。
它被带进一种与原先完全不同的联结之中。
这种改变是按照一个目的、即按照房子的设计而进行的；内在的东西既已与它相一致，外在的东西也就被改造得与之相一致。

en: Animals too have a practical behaviour towards what is external to them.
They act purposefully, that is rationally, out of instinct.
But since they do this unconsciously, one can speak of action in them only in an improper sense.
They have desire and drive, but no rational will.
Of man one also says will of his drive or his desire.

More precisely, however, one distinguishes will from desire; the will, as distinct from proper desire, is then called the higher faculty of desire. - In animals the instinct is distinguished even from their drives and desires themselves, for instinct is indeed an action from desire or drive, but one which is not concluded with its immediate expression, but which still has a further consequence equally necessary for the animal.
It is an action in which a relation also lies to something else; e.g. the dragging of grains by many animals.
This is not yet the whole action, but a purpose lies further out in it, namely their nourishment for the future.
zh: 动物对于与它们外在相关的东西也有一种实践的行为。
它们出于本能而合目的地行动，也就是合乎理性地行动。
但因为它们是无意识地这样做，所以对它们只能说是不严格意义上的行动。
它们有欲求和冲动，但没有理性的意志。
在人的身上，人们也把他的冲动或他的欲求称作意志。
但说得确切些，人们要把意志与欲求区分开；意志有别于真正的欲求，因而随后被称作更高的欲求能力。——在动物那里，连它们的冲动和欲求本身也要与本能区分开，因为本能固然是一种出于欲求或冲动的行为，但它并不随自己的直接表现而完结，而是还另有一种对动物同样必然的后果。
这是一种其上还指向别的什么东西的行为；例如许多动物一起把谷粒拖回去。
这还不是完整的行动，而是其中还有一个指向更远之处的目的，即它们将来的食物。

en: The drive is in the first place something inner, something which begins a movement from itself or brings forth a change out of itself.
The drive proceeds from itself.
It is indeed awakened by external circumstances, but notwithstanding this it was already present.
It is not brought forth by them.

Mechanical causes bring forth merely external or mechanical effects which are completely determined through their causes, in which therefore nothing is contained which was not already present in the cause; e.g. when I impart motion to a body, there is in it nothing but the imparted motion; or when I colour a body, it has nothing further than the imparted colour.
If, by contrast, I act upon a living being, this action makes out of it something quite other than it immediately is.
The efficacy of the living being is thereby excited to show itself out of itself in its own peculiarity.
zh: 冲动首先是一种内在的东西，是某种从自身开始一种运动、或从自身产生一种变化的东西。
冲动从自身出发。
它固然由外在情境唤醒，但即便如此它本来就已经在那里了。
它并不是由此产生出来的。
机械的原因只产生外在的或机械的效果，这些效果完全由它们的原因所规定，因而其中并不包含任何不是已经存在于原因之中的东西；例如当我给一个物体以运动时，其中除了传达过去的运动之外别无他物；或者当我给一个物体染色时，它也就再没有别的，只有那传达过去的颜色。
但如果我作用于一个有生命的存在物，那么这种作用会从它身上造出某种与它直接的样子完全不同的东西。
有生命的存在物的效力由此被激发，从自身出发显示出它自己的特性。

en: Secondly the drive is 1. limited in terms of content, 2. as regards the side of its satisfaction, dependent on external circumstances and hence contingent.
The drive does not go beyond its purpose and is called blind in that respect.
It satisfies itself, whatever the consequences may be.
zh: 其次，冲动 1. 就内容而言是受限制的，2. 就其满足这一面而言，由于依赖外在情境而是偶然的。
冲动不超出它的目的，因而就这一点说是盲目的。
它就满足自己，后果无论是什么样都无所谓。

en: Man does not, in that respect, himself posit his drives, but has them immediately, or they belong to his nature.
Nature, however, is subject to necessity, because everything in it is limited, relative, or simply only in relation to something other.
But what is in relation to something other is not for itself, but dependent on the other.
It has its ground therein and is a necessary something.
Insofar as man has immediately determinate drives, he is subject to nature and behaves as a necessary and unfree being.
zh: 就这一点说，人并不是自己设定自己的冲动，而是直接地具有它们，或者说它们属于他的自然。
但自然服从于必然性，因为自然中的一切都是受限的、相对的，或者干脆只是在与别的东西的关系上才成立的。
但凡是与别的东西有关系的东西，那就不是自为的，而是依赖他者的。
它的根据就在其中，因而是一个必然的东西。
就人直接具有某些有规定的冲动而言，他服从于自然，并作为一个必然的、不自由的存在物而活动。

en: Only man, as a thinking being, can reflect on his drives which in themselves have necessity for him.
Reflection is in general a shortcut [?] away from the immediate.
The reflection of light consists in this: that its rays, which for themselves would propagate in a straight line, are deflected away from this direction. - Spirit has reflection.
It is not bound to the immediate, but is able to go beyond it to something else, - e.g. from an event to the representation of its consequence or of a similar event or even of its cause.
Insofar as spirit steps out beyond something immediate, it has removed the same from itself.
It has reflected into itself.
It has entered into itself.
It has recognised the immediate, insofar as it sets against it another, as something limited.

It is therefore a very great difference whether one merely is or has something, or whether one also knows that one is or has it; e.g. ignorance or roughness of sentiment or of conduct are limitations which one may have without knowing that one has them.
Insofar as one reflects on them or knows of them, one must know their opposite.
Reflection on them is already a first step beyond them.
zh: 唯独人能够作为思维者对他的冲动进行反思——这些冲动自在自为地对他具有必然性。
反思一般说来就是从直接者出发的一种缩短[?]。
光的反射在于：那些本身会以直线传播的光线被从这一方向上偏转开。——精神具有反思。
它不受直接者束缚，而是能够越过直接者走向别的东西——例如从一件事走向对它后果的表象，或走向一件类似的事，甚至走向它的原因。
精神一旦走向某个直接的东西，它就把同一个东西从自己这里移开了。
它在自己之中反思了自己。
它进入了自己内部。
就它给直接者提出另一个对立物而言，它把直接者认作一个受限制的东西。
因此，一个人是仅仅为某物或具有某物，还是也知道自己是某物或具有某物，这之间有着极大的差别；例如，无知或心态与举止的粗野都是一些限制，人们可以具有它们却并不知道自己具有它们。
就人对它们进行反思或知道它们而言，他就必须知道它们的反面。
对它们的反思已经是越过它们的第一步。

en: Drives as natural determinations are limitations.
It is through reflection on them that man in general begins to go beyond them.

The first reflection concerns here the means: whether they are appropriate to the drive, whether the drive is thereby satisfied; further, whether the means are not too important to be sacrificed for this drive.
zh: 冲动作为自然的规定就是限制。
人正是通过对它们的反思开始超出它们。
这里最初的反思涉及手段：这些手段是否与冲动相适应，冲动是否由此得到满足；此外还要看这些手段是否并非重要到不能为这个冲动而牺牲它们。

en: Reflection compares the various drives and their purposes with the fundamental purpose of the being.
The purposes of the particular drives are limited, but each of them in its own way contributes to the fundamental purpose being attained.
Yet one of them is more closely related to it than the other.
Reflection has therefore to compare the drives as to whether they are related to the fundamental purpose and whether the same is promoted more by their satisfaction.
In reflection the transition begins from the lower faculty of desire to the higher.
Man is therein no longer mere natural being, or no longer stands in the sphere of necessity.
Something is necessary insofar as only this and not something else can happen.
Before reflection there stands not only the one immediate object but also another or its opposite.
zh: 反思把各种不同的冲动及其目的与存在者的基本目的相比较。
特殊冲动的目的是受限的，但每一个都以自己的方式有助于基本目的的达成。
然而其中这个比那个与它更为亲近。
所以反思要比较这些冲动，看它们是否与基本目的相亲近，以及它们各自的满足是否更能促进这个基本目的。
在反思中，从低级欲求能力向更高级者的过渡开始了。
人在其中不再只是自然存在物，也不再处在必然性的领域里。
某物是必然的，就在于只可能发生这个而不可能发生别的。
在反思之前，面前有的不只是一个直接的对象，还有另一个对象或它的反面。
