en: The reflection just described, however, is properly only a relative one.

It does indeed go beyond something finite, but always comes back again to something finite; e.g. when we go beyond one place in space, another, larger one presents itself to us, but it is always a limited space or place, and so it goes on to infinity.
Likewise, when we go back from the present time into the past, we can represent to ourselves a period of ten thousand or even thirty thousand years.
Such reflection does indeed proceed from one determinate point in space, in time, to another, but it does not emerge out of space or out of time itself.
So it is also in practical-relative reflection.
It leaves an immediate inclination, desire or drive and passes to another drive, desire or inclination, leaves this one again too, and so on.
Insofar as it is relative, it merely falls back again and again into a drive, merely keeps moving about in desires, and does not rise above this whole sphere of drives.
zh: 但刚才所描述的这种反思其实只是一种相对的反思。
它固然越过某个有限者，但又总是回到某个有限者；例如当我们越过空间中的一个地点时，面前会设想出另一个更大的地点，但它总是一个受限制的空间或地点，如此一直延续到无限。
同样，当我们越过当前的时间而回到过去时，我们可以设想出一个一万年、乃至三万年的时期。
这样的反思固然是从空间中、时间中的某个确定之点走向另一个点，但它并没有走出空间本身或时间本身。
在实践的—相对的反思中情形也是如此。
它离开一种直接的倾向、欲求或冲动，走向另一个冲动、欲求或倾向，又再次离开这个，如此等等。
就它是相对而言，它只是一再落回某个冲动之中，只是在种种欲求里打转，并不超出这整个冲动的领域。

en: Practical absolute reflection, however, rises above this whole sphere of the finite or leaves the sphere of the lower faculty of desire in which man is determined by nature and dependent on what is external.
Finiteness consists in general in this: that something has a limit, that is, that its non-being is posited here or that it ceases here, that it therefore relates itself here to something other.
Infinite reflection, by contrast, consists in this: that I no longer relate myself to something other but to myself, or that I am my own object.
This pure relation to myself is the I, the root of the infinite being itself.
It is the complete abstraction from everything finite.
The I as such has no content given by nature or immediate, but has only itself as content.
This pure form is at the same time its own content.

Every content given by nature is 1. something limited: the I, by contrast, is unlimited; 2. the content of nature is immediate: the pure I, by contrast, has no immediate content, because it is only through the abstraction from everything other.
zh: 但实践的绝对反思却超出这整个有限者的领域，或者离开了低级欲求能力的领域——人在其中由自然所规定并依赖外在者。
有限性总的说来在于：某物有一个界限，也就是说，它在这里的非存在被设定，或者它在这里终止，因而它由此也就与别的什么东西相关。
但无限的反思在于：我不再与别的什么东西相关，而是与我自己相关，或者说，我对自己而言就是对象。
这种纯粹的对自我的关系就是自我，它是无限的存在者本身的根基。
它是对一切有限者的完全抽象。
自我作为这样的自我没有任何由自然给予的或直接的内容，而只把自己当作内容。
这种纯粹的形式同时就是它自己的内容。
每一个由自然给予的内容 1. 都是某种受限制的东西；而自我却是不受限制的；2. 自然的内容是直接的；而纯粹的自我则没有任何直接的内容，因为它只有通过从一切别的东西中抽象出来才存在。

en: To begin with the I is the purely indeterminate.
But it can through its reflection pass over from indeterminacy to determinacy, for example to seeing, hearing etc.
In this determinacy it has become unequal to itself, but at the same time it has remained in its indeterminacy, that is, it can, by entering into it, return again into itself.

Resolve too belongs here, for reflection precedes it and it consists in this: that I have several determinacies before me, in indeterminate number, which must yet at least be these two, namely some determinacy of something or else not this.
Resolve sublates reflection, the passing over and back from one to another; it fixes a determinacy and makes it its own.
The basic condition of resolving, of the possibility of resolving oneself or of reflecting before acting, is the absolute indeterminacy of the I.
zh: 首先，自我是纯粹不定性的。
但它可以通过自己的反思从不定性过渡到规定性，例如过渡到看、听等等。
在这种规定性中它变得与自身不再相等，但它同时仍留在自己的不定性中，也就是说，它一旦进入其中，就能重新返回自身。
决心也属于这里，因为反思在它之前，而决心在于：我面前有若干个规定性，数量不确定，但它们至少必须是这两个，即对某物的一个规定，或者甚至不是这个。
决心扬弃反思，扬弃从一个到另一个的来回往返；它把一个规定性固定下来，并把它变成自己的。
决心的基本条件，即能够下决心或能够在行动之前进行反思的可能性，就是自我的绝对不定性。

en: The freedom of the will is freedom in general, and all other freedoms are merely species of it.
When one says "freedom of the will", one does not mean that there is beside the will also some power, property or capacity which also has freedom.
Just as when one speaks of the omnipotence of God one does not understand it as though there were besides him other beings which had omnipotence.
There is therefore civil freedom, freedom of the press, political freedom, religious freedom.
These species of freedom are the general concept of freedom insofar as it is applied to particular relations or objects.

Religious freedom consists in this: that religious representations, religious actions are not forced upon me, that is, that only such determinations are in it which I acknowledge as mine, which I make my own.

A religion which is forced upon me, or in view of which I do not behave as a free being, is not mine, but always remains foreign to me. - The political freedom of a people consists in constituting a state of its own and in deciding what counts as the general national will either by the whole people itself or by those who belong to the people and whom it can acknowledge as its own, in that every other citizen has equal rights with them.
zh: 意志的自由就是一般的自由，而所有其他的自由都不过是它的种类。
当人们说「意志的自由」时，并不是说在意志之外还有某种力量、性质或能力也具有自由。
正如当人们谈到上帝的全能时，并不是说除他之外还有别的存在物具有全能。
所以有公民自由、出版自由、政治自由和宗教自由。
自由的这些种类就是一般的自由概念，就它被应用于特殊的关系或对象而言。
宗教自由在于：宗教表象、宗教行动不被强加于我；也就是说，其中只有那些我认作自己的规定，即我把它们变成自己的规定。
一种被强加于我的宗教，或者一种我据此不能以自由存在者的方式行事的宗教，就不是我的宗教，而始终是我的一种外在的宗教。——一个民族的政治自由在于：构成一个自己的国家，并且把那种被视为普遍的国家意志的东西，或者由整个民族亲自决定，或者由属于这个民族的人来决定——只要每个其他公民与他们享有同等权利，这个民族就可以把他们认作自己的人。

en: One will perhaps express it thus: my will has been determined by these motives, circumstances, attractions and drives.
This expression contains in the first place that I have behaved passively in it.
But in truth I have not only behaved passively but essentially actively in it, namely in this: that my will has taken up these circumstances as motives, allowed them to count as motives.
The causal relation does not obtain here.
The circumstances do not behave as causes and my will not as their effect.
According to this relation, what lies in the cause must necessarily occur.
As reflection, however, I can go beyond every determination which is posited through the circumstances.

Insofar as man appeals to the fact that he has been seduced by circumstances, attractions etc., he wants with that to shove the action away from himself as it were, but with it merely lowers himself to an unfree or natural being, whereas his action is in truth always his own, not that of another and not the effect of something outside him.
The circumstances or motives have only so much dominion over man as he himself grants them.
zh: 人们大概会这样表述：我的意志是被这些动机、情境、诱惑和冲动所决定的。
这种表述首先包含着：我在其中是被动地活动的。
但实际上我在其中并不只是被动地，而且本质上也是主动地活动的，即在于我的意志把这些情境接纳为动机，把它们看作动机。
在这里并不存在因果关系。
情境并不作为原因而活动，我的意志也不是作为它们的效果。
按照这种关系，凡在原因之中的东西就必然发生。
但作为反思，我能超出由情境所设定的每一个规定。
就人以「自己是被情境、诱惑等等引诱的」这一点作为根据而言，他是想以此把行动仿佛从自己身上推开；但他这样做只是把自己降低为一个不自由的或自然的存在物，其实他的行动始终是他自己的行动，不是别人的行动，也不是他之外某种东西的效果。
情境或动机对人拥有的支配力，只等于他自己承认给它们的那一份。

en: The determinations of the lower faculty of desire are determinations of nature.
Insofar as this is so, it seems neither necessary nor possible that man should make them his own.
Yet precisely as determinations of nature they do not yet belong to his will or his freedom, for the essence of his will is that nothing be in it which he has not himself made his own.

He is therefore able to consider that which belongs to his nature as something alien, so that it is accordingly only in him, only belongs to him, insofar as he makes it his own or follows his natural drives with resolve.
zh: 低级欲求能力的那些规定是自然的规定。
就此而言，人似乎既不必要也不可能是把它们变成自己的规定。
但正因为它们是自然的规定，它们就还不属于他的意志或他的自由；因为他意志的本质在于：其中没有任何不是他自己变成自己之物的内容。
所以他能够把属于他的自然的东西当作某个外在的东西来看待；因此它只在他里面、只属于他，就这一点说，即他把它变成自己的，或者他以决心追随自己的自然冲动。

en: To impute the guilt of an action to a person means imputing or reckoning it to him.
One cannot yet impute any action to children who are still in the state of nature; they are not yet capable of imputation; the same applies to madmen or the feeble-minded.
zh: 把一项行动的罪责归到一个人身上，就是把这罪责归责于他、算在他头上。
对还处在自然状态的孩子，人们还不能归责任何行动；他们还不具备归责能力；疯人或心智薄弱者同样如此。

en: In the difference between deed and action lies the difference of the concepts of guilt as they occur in the tragic representations of the ancients and in our own concepts.
In the former the deed is attributed to the person according to its whole compass.
He has to make amends for the whole, and no distinction is made that he knew only one side of the deed but not the others.
He is here represented as an absolute knowing altogether, not merely as a relative and contingent one; or that which he does is regarded altogether as his deed.

No part is rolled off him onto another being; e.g. Ajax, when in the madness of his anger at not having received the weapons of Achilles, he killed the cattle and sheep of the Greeks, did not shove the guilt onto his madness as though in it he were another being, but he took the whole action upon himself as the doer and put himself out of the world from shame.
zh: 行为与行动之间的差别中，蕴含着罪责概念上的差别——这些概念既见于古代的悲剧演出中，也见于我们自己的概念中。
在古代的演出中，行为按其全部范围被归到人身上。
他必须为整体受罚，而且人们并不区分他只知道行为的一个方面而不知道其他方面。
这里他被表现为一种绝对的知，而不是仅仅一种相对的、偶然的知；或者说，他所做的事情总归被看作他的行为。
人们并不把其中一部分从他身上卸下、推到另一个存在物身上；例如埃阿斯在因未得到阿喀琉斯武器的愤怒而发疯时杀死了希腊人的牛羊，他并没有把罪责推给自己的疯癫，仿佛在疯癫中他是另一个存在物，而是他作为行为人把整个行动承担到自己身上，并因羞愧而自戕。

en: If the will were not a universal, there would be no proper laws, nothing that could truly oblige everyone.
Everyone could act according to his own pleasure and would not respect the arbitrariness of another.
That the will is a universal follows from the concept of its freedom.
Men, considered as they appear, show themselves as very different with respect to the will in general, according to character, custom, inclination and particular capacities.
They are in that respect particular individuals and differ from one another by nature.
Each has capacities and determinations in himself which the other lacks.
These differences of individuals concern the will in itself in no way, because it is free.
Freedom consists precisely in the indeterminacy of the will, or [in the fact] that it has no natural determinacy in itself.
The will in itself is therefore a universal will.
The particularity or individuality of man does not stand in the way of the universality of the will, but is subordinate to it.
An action which is right or moral or otherwise excellent is indeed performed by a single individual, but everyone agrees with it.
They therefore recognise themselves or their own will in it. - Here it is the same case as with works of art.
Even those who would not have been able to produce such a work find their own essence expressed in it.
Such a work therefore shows itself as truly universal.
The more the particularity of the author has vanished from it, the greater the applause it receives.
zh: 如果意志不是一个普遍者，那就不会有真正的规律，也不会有任何能真正约束所有人的东西。
每个人都可以随心所欲地行动，而不会尊重他人的任意。
意志是普遍者这一点，源自其自由的概念。
人们就其外观来看，就意志总体而言，在性格、习俗、倾向和特殊天资方面显得彼此非常不同。
就此而言，他们是个别的个体，并且彼此在自然上相区别。
每一个都有自己所缺乏于他人的天资与规定。
个体的这些差别与自在的意志毫不相干，因为它是自由的。
自由恰恰就在于意志的不定性，或者[在于]它自身不含任何自然的规定性。
所以自在的意志就是普遍意志。
人的特殊性或个别性并不妨碍意志的普遍性，而是从属于它。
一个在法权上、道德上或在其他方面卓越的行动，虽然是由某一个人做出的，但所有人都赞同它。
所以他们在其中认出了自己或他们自己的意志。——这里的情形与艺术作品的情形相同。
即使那些本来不可能创造出这样一件作品的人，也在其中发现表达了他们自己的本质。
所以这样一件作品显示为真正普遍的。
作者的特殊性从中消失得越多，它得到的赞同就越大。

en: It can be the case that one is not conscious of one’s general will.
A man can believe that something goes completely against his will, even though it is after all his will.
The criminal who is punished may indeed wish that the punishment be turned away from him; but the general will carries it along that the crime be punished.
It must therefore be assumed that it lies in the absolute will of the criminal himself that he be punished.

Insofar as he is punished, the demand is present that he also see that he is being justly punished, and if he sees it, he may indeed wish to be free of the punishment as from an external suffering; but insofar as he admits that he is being justly punished, his general will agrees with the punishment.
zh: 可能的情况是：一个人意识不到自己的普遍意志。
人可能以为某件事完全违背自己的意志，其实它恰恰就是他的意志。
被刑罚的犯罪者固然可能希望刑罚从他身上免除；但普遍意志本身就包含着犯罪要受刑罚这一点。
因此必须假定：犯罪者受罚这一点就包含在他自己的绝对意志之中。
就他受罚而言，就要求他也能看出自己受到的是公正的处罚；而当他看出这一点时，他固然可能希望自己作为摆脱一种外在的痛苦而免于刑罚，但就他承认自己受到公正处罚而言，他的普遍意志是赞同刑罚的。

en: Arbitrariness is freedom, but it is formal freedom, or freedom insofar as my will relates itself to something limited.
One must distinguish two sides here: 1. insofar as the will does not remain in equality with itself, and 2. insofar as it does remain in equality with itself.
zh: 任意是自由，但它是形式的自由，或者说，它是就我的意志与某个受限制的东西相关的意义上的自由。
在这里必须区分两个方面：1. 就意志在其中不与自身等同而言，2. 就意志在其中与自身等同而言。

en: ad 1.
Insofar as the will wants something, it has a determinate, limited content.
It is therefore unequal with itself insofar as it is here genuinely determinate but is indeterminate in and for itself.
The limited which it has taken into itself is thus something other than itself; e.g. if I want to go or to see, then I am a goer or a seer.
I therefore behave unequally with myself, because going or seeing is something limited and not
zh: ad 1.
就意志想要某物而言，它就有了一个有规定的、受限制的内容。
所以就此而言，它与自身处于不平等之中，因为它在这里确实是有规定的，而自在自为地却是无规定的。
所以他所接纳进自身的那受限制的东西，是与他自己不同的另一个东西；例如当我想行走或观看时，我就是一个行走者或观看者。
所以我与自身处于不平等之中，因为行走或观看是某种受限制的东西，并且不

en: equal to the I.
zh: 等同于自我。

en: ad 2.

But I behave in equality with myself, or freely, in form as well here, because in being determined in this way I at the same time look upon it as something alien, or distinguish this determinacy from myself, the I, because to go and to see in this way is not in me by nature, but because I myself have posited it within my will.
Insofar as this is so, it is obviously at the same time not alien either, because I have made it my own and in it have my will for myself.
zh: ad 2.
但我在这里就形式而言也与自身等同，或者说也是自由的，因为我既这样是有规定的，就同时把这个规定看成某个外在的东西，或者把这规定性与我自己、这个自我区分开，因为这样去行走、去观看并不是出于自然在我之内，而是因为我自己把它设定进了我的意志。
就此而言，它显然同时也不是一个外在的东西，因为我把它变成了我的，并且在其中对自己拥有我的意志。

en: This freedom is therefore a formal freedom, because along with the equality with myself there is also present inequality with me, or a limited something in me.

When we speak of freedom in common life, we usually understand by it arbitrariness or relative freedom, that I can do something or also leave it undone. - With a limited will we can have formal freedom insofar as we distinguish this determinate thing from us or reflect on it, that is, insofar as we are also beyond it. - When we are in passion or act driven by nature, we have no formal freedom.
Because our I dissolves entirely into this feeling, it does not appear to us to be something limited.
Our I is not also at the same time outside it, does not distinguish itself from it.
zh: 这种自由于是是一种形式的自由，因为在与自身等同的同时，也同时存在与自身的不等同，或者说在我之内有某个受限制的东西。
当我们在日常生活中说到自由时，通常把它理解为任意或相对的自由，即我可以做某事也可以不做。——在意志受限制的情况下，我们能够有形式的自由，就我们把这个规定的东西从自身区分出来或对它进行反思而言，也就是说，就我们还超出它而言。——当我们处在激情中、或者受自然驱动而行动时，我们就没有形式的自由。
由于我们的自我完全消失在这种感觉之中，它在我们看来就不是某个受限制的东西。
我们的自我并没有同时在它之外，也没有与它相区别。

en: The absolutely free will differs from the relatively free will, or arbitrariness, in that the absolute has only itself for its object, whereas the relative has something limited.
For the relative will, e.g. desire, it is only a matter of the object.
The absolute, however, also differs from self-will.
This has in common with the absolute will that it is not so much a matter of the matter itself as rather of the will as will, that precisely its will be respected.
The two are indeed to be distinguished.

The self-willed stays with his will purely because it is his will, without having a rational ground for it, i.e. without his will being something of general validity. - As necessary as it is to have strength of will which perseveres in a rational purpose, so contrary to reason is self-will, because it is the wholly individual and exclusive thing against others.
The truly free will has no contingent content.
Only it itself is not contingent.
zh: 绝对自由的意志与相对自由的意志即任意相区别在于：绝对的只以自己为对象，而相对的那个则以某个受限制的东西为对象。
对相对的那个意志、例如欲求来说，关心的只是对象。
但绝对的还与自作主张相区别。
后者与绝对的意志共有的地方在于：它所关心的与其说是事情本身，不如说是意志作为意志本身，即恰恰要它的意志得到尊重。
两者固然要区分开来。
自作主张者之所以坚守自己的意志，纯粹是因为这就是他的意志，并没有为此提供一个理性的根据，也就是说，他的意志并不是某个普遍有效的东西。——正如具有坚持理性目的的意志力量是必要的，自作主张同样是令人厌恶的，因为它是完全个别和排他的东西，是针对他人的。
真正自由的意志没有偶然的内容。
只有它自己才是不偶然的。

en: For the pure will it is not a matter of any particularity.
Insofar as this is the case with the will, it is arbitrariness, for this has a limited interest and takes its determinations from natural drives and inclinations.
Such a content is given and not absolutely posited through the will.
The principle of the will is therefore that its freedom come about and be preserved.
Besides, it indeed wants still many various determinations.

It has still many determinate purposes, institutions, conditions etc.; but these are not purposes of the will in and for itself, rather they are purposes because they are means and conditions for the realisation of the freedom of the will, which makes institutions and laws necessary for the limitation of arbitrariness, of inclination and of mere caprice, and in general of the drives and desires which relate merely to natural purposes; e.g. education has the purpose of making man an independent being, that is, a being of free will.
For this intention many limitations of their pleasure are imposed on children.
They must learn to obey, so that their individual or private will, and further their dependence on sensuous inclinations and desires, is sublated and their will thus liberated.
zh: 纯粹的意志所关心的不是任何一种特殊性。
就意志上是这样情形而言，它就是任意，因为任意有一个受限制的利益，并且是从自然的冲动与倾向中取得自己的规定的。
这样的内容是给定的，并不是绝对地由意志设定出来的。
所以意志的原则就是：使它的自由得以成立并得以保持。
此外它固然还想要各种各样的规定。
它还有各种各样的确定目的、设施和状态等等，但这些并不是自在自为地属于意志的目的，而是它们之所以为目的，是因为它们是实现意志自由的手段与条件；这一自由使得为限制任意、倾向和单纯的随意——总之为限制那些仅仅关乎自然目的的冲动与欲求——成为必要的设施与法律；例如，教育的目的就是把人造就成一个独立自主的存在者，也就是一个具有自由意志的存在者。
为了这一意图，人们给孩子们加上了各种各样的对其欲望的限制。
他们必须学会服从，以便他们个别的或私有的意志以及对感性倾向与欲求的依赖被扬弃，从而他们的意志得到解放。

en: Man is a free being.
This constitutes the basic determination of his nature.
Besides, however, he has still other necessary needs, particular purposes and drives, e.g. the drive to know, to preserve his life, his health etc.
Right does not have man for its object according to these particular determinations.
It has not the purpose of promoting him according to them or of rendering him a particular help in respect of them.
zh: 人是自由的存在者。
这构成了他的自然的基本规定。
但除此之外，他还有别的必然需要、特殊目的和冲动，例如求认识的冲动、保存自己生命与健康的冲动等等。
法并不是按照这些特殊规定才把人当作对象的。
它的目的并不是按照这些规定来促进他，或为此对他提供特别的帮助。

en: Secondly.
Right does not depend on the intention one has in it.
One can do something with a very good intention, but the action does not thereby become lawful, but can notwithstanding be unlawful.

On the other hand an action, e.g. the assertion of my property, can be perfectly lawful and yet have a bad intention in it, in that for me it is not merely a matter of right, but rather a matter of harming the other.
On right as such this intention has no influence.
zh: 第二。
法并不取决于人们在这当中抱有什么意图。
人们可以抱着非常好的意图去做某事，但这个行为并不会因此就合法，反而不顾这一点仍可能是不法的。
另一方面，一个行为、例如主张我的财产，可以完全合法，而在其中却抱着恶意的意图，因为我所关心的并不只是权利，而更在于损害对方。
对法本身而言，这种意图并没有影响。

en: Thirdly.
It does not depend on the conviction whether what I have to perform is right or wrong.
This is especially the case with punishment.
One will indeed seek to convince the criminal that right is done him.
Yet this conviction or non-conviction has no influence on the right that is done him.
zh: 第三。
我所应当履行的是正当还是不正当，并不取决于确信。
在刑罚的情形中尤其如此。
人们大概会试图说服犯罪者，使他确信自己受到的是正当的对待。
但这种确信或不信对他所受到的对待没有影响。

en: Finally, right also does not depend on the disposition with which something is carried out.

It is very often the case that one does right merely out of fear of the punishment or out of fear of other unpleasant consequences in general, e.g. of losing one’s good name or one’s credit; or one can also, while fulfilling one’s right, have the disposition of being rewarded for it in the other life.
Right as such, however, is independent of these dispositions.
zh: 最后，法同样也不取决于某件事是以何种心态完成的。
常常有这样的情形：人们纯粹出于对刑罚的恐惧、或者对其他一切不利后果的恐惧（例如害怕失去自己的好名声、自己的信用）而履行自己的法；或者人们也可以在履行自己的权利时抱着这样的心态：在来世为此得到奖赏。
但法本身是与这些心态无关的。

en: Right and morality are distinguished from one another.
According to right something may well be permitted which morality forbids.
Right, for example, allows me to dispose of my property in a wholly indeterminate way, but morality contains determinations which limit the same.

It may seem as if morality permitted much which right does not permit; but morality not only requires the observance of right towards others, rather it adds to right the disposition to respect right for right’s sake.
Morality itself requires that right be observed first, and where it ceases, moral determinations enter.
zh: 法与道德是彼此区分的。
就法而言，某件事完全可以是允许的，而道德却禁止它。
例如，法允许我完全不受限制地处分我的财产，然而道德却包含着限制这种处分的规定。
看上去似乎道德允许许多法所不允许的事；然而道德所要求的不仅是对他人遵守法，而且是在法之外再加上一种心态，即为了法本身就尊重法。
道德本身就要求首先遵守法；而在法终止之处，道德的规定就登场了。

en: In order that an action have moral value, insight is necessary as to whether it is right or wrong, good or evil.
What one calls the innocence of children or of uncivilised nations is not yet morality.

Children or such nations refrain from a great many evil actions because they have no conception of it, because in general the relations under which alone such actions become possible are not yet present; such refraining from evil actions has no moral value.

But they also do actions which are in accordance with morality and are therefore nevertheless not really moral, insofar as they have no insight into the nature of the action, whether it is good or evil.
zh: 一个行为要有道德上的价值，就必须洞见它是正当还是不正当、是善还是恶。
人们所谓的儿童或未开化民族的天真，还不是道德。
儿童或这样的民族不做许多恶的行为，是因为他们对此还没有任何表象，因为总的说来，那些唯有在其下这类行为才成为可能的关系还不存在；这样不做恶的行为并没有道德上的价值。
但他们也做出符合道德的行为，而正因如此它们却并不真正是道德的，因为他们对行为的本性——它是善还是恶——并没有洞见。

en: Opposed to one’s own conviction stands mere faith on the authority of others.
If my action is to have moral value, my conviction must be connected with it.
The action must be mine in the full sense.
But if I act on the authority of others, it is not entirely mine; it is a foreign conviction which acts out of me.
zh: 与自己的确信相对立的是对他人权威的单纯信仰。
如果我的行为要有道德上的价值，那么我的确信就必须与它相联结。
这个行为必须在完整的意义上是我自己的。
但如果我依据他人的权威而行动，那么它就并不完全是我自己的；是一个外来的确信在替我行动。

en: But there are also relations in which it is the moral side precisely to act out of obedience and on the authority of others.

Originally man follows his natural inclinations without deliberation or with reflections which are still one-sided, crooked and incorrect, and which themselves still stand under the rule of sensuousness.
In this state he must learn to obey, because his will is not yet the rational one.
Through this obedience the negative comes about, that he learns to renounce sensuous desire, and only through this obedience does man attain independence.
In this sphere he always follows another, just as much when he obeys his own will, which is as a whole still sensuous, as when he obeys the will of another.

As a natural being he stands on the one hand under the rule of external things; on the other hand however these inclinations and desires are something immediate, limited, unfree, or something other than his true will.
Obedience to the law of reason is obedience in relation to my inessential nature, which stands under the rule of an other for it.
But on the other side it is independent determination out of itself, for precisely this law has its root in my essence.
zh: 但也存在一些关系，在其中恰恰是出于服从并依据他人的权威去行动，才算是道德的一面。
起初，人是不加考虑地、或只带着那些仍属片面的、偏曲的和不正确的、甚至仍处在感性支配之下的反思，去追随他的自然倾向。
在这种状态中他必须学会服从，因为他的意志还不是理性的意志。
通过这种服从就产生了否定的一面：他学会了放弃感性的欲求；而人只有通过这种服从才达到独立自主。
在这一领域中他总是追随另一个东西，无论他服从的是他自己那个总体上还感性的意志，还是别人的意志。
作为自然存在物，他一方面处在外在事物的支配之下；另一方面，这些倾向与欲求乃是一种直接的东西、受限制的东西、不自由的东西，是某个不同于他真正意志的东西。
对理性法则的服从，是就我的非本质的自然而言的服从，而这自然处在一个对它而言的他者的支配之下。
但另一方面，它是出自信自的独立的规定，因为恰恰这条法则的根基就在我的本质之中。

en: The disposition is therefore in morality an essential moment.
It consists in this: that one does one’s duty because it is so fitting.
It is therefore an unmoral disposition to do something out of fear of punishment or in order to retain a good opinion of oneself with others.

This is a heterogeneous, i.e. alien, motive, for it is not the ground of the matter itself, or else one then does not regard right as something which is in and for itself, but as something which depends on external determinations.
zh: 所以心态在道德中是一个本质的环节。
它在于人们因为事情本来就该如此而履行义务。
所以，出于对刑罚的恐惧、或者为了在别人那里保住对自己的一种好印象而去做某事，都是一种不道德的心态。
这是一种异质的、也就是外来的动机，因为它不是事情本身的根据；或者说，人们这时并不把法看作自在自为的东西，而是把它看作某种依赖外在规定的东西。

en: Nevertheless the consideration whether penalties or rewards are set upon an action is of importance, even though the consequences do not constitute the value of the action.

The consequences of a good action can often draw much evil after it, whereas an evil action can also have good among its consequences. - But to think in general of the consequences of the action is important for this reason, that one thereby does not remain at the immediate point of view but goes beyond it.
Through their many-sided consideration one is also led to the nature of actions.
zh: 尽管后果并不构成行为的价值，但考察一个行为上是否系着刑罚或奖赏，仍然是重要的。
一个善的行为的后果往往可能招致许多祸害，而一个恶的行为在其后果中同样也可能有好的。——但总的说来去思考行为的后果之所以重要，是因为人由此不会停留在直接的着眼点上，而是超出它。
通过它的多方面考察，人们也会被引向行为的本性。

en: According to right man is to man an object as an absolutely free being; according to morality, by contrast, as an individual according to his particular determinate being, as a member of the family, as a friend, as such a character etc.
If the external circumstances in which man stands with others are such that he fulfils his determination, then that is his fortune.
On the one hand this well-being lies in the power of his will; on the other hand it depends on external circumstances and other men.

Morality also has man for its object according to his particular determinate being or his well-being, and requires not only that man be left in his abstract freedom but also that his well-being be promoted. - Well-being as the adequacy of the external to our inner we also call pleasure.

Beatitude is not only a single pleasure but a lasting condition, in part of the actual pleasure itself, in part also of the circumstances and means by which one always has the possibility to create pleasure for oneself if one will.
The latter is therefore the pleasure of the representation.
In beatitude, however, as in pleasure, the concept of fortune lies, that it is contingent whether the external circumstances are adequate to the inner determinations of the drives.
Beatitude, by contrast, consists in this: that no fortune is in it, i.e. that in it the adequacy of the external determinate being to the inner desire is not contingent.
Beatitude can be said only of God, in whom willing and accomplishing his absolute power are the same.
For man, however, the accord of the external with his inner is limited and contingent.
In it he is dependent.
zh: 按照法，人对人是作为绝对自由的存在者而成为对象的；按照道德，人对人则是作为按照其特殊定在的一个个别者——作为家庭成员、作为朋友、作为这样的一种性格等等——而成为对象的。
如果一个人与他人相处其中的外在情境恰好能使他实现自己的规定，那么那就是他的幸运。
一方面这份福祉处在他意志的掌握之中，另一方面它又依赖外在情境与他人。
道德同样把按照其特殊定在、或按照其福祉的人当作对象；它不仅要求让一个人在抽象的自由中不受干预，而且也要求他的福祉得到促进。——我们把作为外在与我们内在之相宜的幸福也称为快乐。
至福不仅仅是一种单独的快乐，而是一种持续的状态：一部分来自快乐本身，一部分也来自那些情境与手段，借由它们人总是有可能在自己愿意时创造出快乐。
后者因此就是表象的快乐。
但在至福中如同在快乐中一样，都包含着幸运的概念：外在情境是否与冲动内在的规定相相宜，是偶然的。
相反，至福在于其中没有运气，也就是说，在其中外在定在与内在欲求的相宜并不是偶然的。
至福只能对上帝说，因为在意欲与实现其绝对威力这两者之中是同一个东西。
但对人来说，外在与他内在的相符是受限的、偶然的。
他在其中是依赖的。

en: The moral will in respect of the disposition is imperfect.

It is a will which has the goal of perfection, but 1. it is driven towards its attainment also by the motive power of sensuousness and individuality, 2. it does not have the means in its power and is therefore limited in bringing about the well-being of others.

In religion, by contrast, one contemplates the divine being, the completion of the will according to its two sides, namely according to the perfection of the disposition, which no longer has in it alien motive powers, and then according to the perfection of the power to attain the holy purposes.
zh: 就心态而言，道德的意志是不完美的。
它是一个以完满为目标的意志，但 1. 为了达到这个目标，它也受到感性与个别性这一动力的驱使，2. 它并不掌握这些手段，因此使他人的福祉得以成就这件事，对它是受限的。
相反，在宗教中人们考察的是上帝这一存在者，即意志从它两个方面所达到的完成：首先是心态的完满——它之内不再有外来的动力；其次是力量的完满——那实现神圣目的的力量。
